title: Website design
summary: Website design starts with what your visitors need to find, understand and do. We organise the pages and content, establish the visual direction and deliver responsive Figma layouts ready for development.
useCases: A new business needs a clear, credible first website.
An existing site looks inconsistent or makes the offer hard to understand.
A marketing team needs reusable page patterns instead of isolated mockups.

work.title: Page structure and content
work.detail: We map the audience, important questions and primary actions, then build a sitemap and wireframes. Navigation, service explanations, enquiry paths and content priorities are reviewed together so the design supports a real customer journey.
work.check: Walk through key tasks, such as finding a service and making an enquiry. Check that each page has a clear purpose and that important information is reachable.

work.title: Responsive visual system
work.detail: We define typography, colour, spacing, grids, image direction and reusable components. Desktop and mobile layouts cover agreed page types, including long headings, different content lengths and realistic images rather than idealised placeholder content.
work.check: Review narrow and wide layouts, text contrast, readable line lengths, image crops and consistent components across the agreed screen inventory.

work.title: Interactions and engineering handover
work.detail: We specify menus, buttons, forms, hover and focus behaviour, loading feedback and error states. A linked prototype demonstrates the priority journeys. Behaviour notes explain what changes at each breakpoint and which animations need a reduced-motion alternative.
work.check: Review the prototype with engineering and record unresolved behaviours. Confirm that assets, component states and responsive rules are understandable without guessing.

technology.name: Figma and component libraries
technology.detail: Shared components, variants and named styles keep the layouts consistent and make future page designs easier to maintain. Editable design files form part of the agreed handover.

technology.name: Design tokens
technology.detail: Documented colour, spacing, type and radius values provide a bridge to CSS variables or a frontend token system. Tokens are organised by purpose, such as text, surfaces and actions.

technology.name: Responsive and accessible interaction patterns
technology.detail: We consider content order, keyboard focus, contrast and touch targets during design. A design review informs implementation; accessibility also needs to be verified in the finished website.

deliverables: Exported assets and an engineering handover
inputs: Your business goals, audiences and primary enquiry or purchase action.
Existing logo files, brand guidelines, copy, photographs and usage permissions.
An agreed page list and a decision-maker who can consolidate feedback.
process: Understand
Review the offer, audience, content and current site. Agree page types, responsibilities and review criteria.
Structure
Approve the sitemap and wireframes before investing in detailed visual design.
Design and review
Develop the visual direction, responsive pages and prototype using realistic content.
Prepare for build
Resolve implementation questions and package components, assets and behaviour notes.
faq: Does website design include development?
This service covers planning and design. Development can be added as a connected workstream, with implementation, CMS and launch responsibilities agreed separately.
Can you work with our existing brand?
Yes. We can apply an existing identity or propose a focused digital refresh. A complete rebrand belongs in a separately agreed brand-identity scope.
overview: Sitemaps, responsive layouts, prototypes and a documented design handover.

title: Web development
summary: We build business websites and web applications, from content-managed sites to customer portals. The work includes the interface, CMS, APIs and integrations your project needs, with source code and setup documentation at handover.
useCases: A marketing website needs dependable content editing and lead capture.
A product needs authenticated workflows or connections to external systems.
An existing website needs a maintainable rebuild or a staged migration.

work.title: Frontend and content architecture
work.detail: We build reusable page templates, semantic layouts and responsive components. Content models define the fields editors actually need. Rendering, image delivery and caching choices follow the content's freshness requirements and the way visitors use the site.
work.check: Verify routes, editing workflows, navigation and key journeys at agreed screen sizes. Check loading, empty and error states as well as the finished content.

work.title: Data, authentication and integrations
work.detail: We define request and response contracts, validate input on the server and enforce permissions where data is accessed. Integrations include clear timeout, retry and duplicate-submission behaviour so a failed upstream service does not produce a misleading success message.
work.check: Test invalid input, unauthorised access, expired sessions, failed external requests and repeated submissions. Confirm that secrets remain outside browser-delivered code.

work.title: Release and maintainability
work.detail: Development, staging and production configuration are separated. We document environment variables, builds, deployment and rollback. Performance work targets the actual page mix and critical journeys instead of relying on one artificial score.
work.check: Run the agreed functional checks on staging, inspect accessibility and performance findings, and confirm who owns deployment, backups and post-launch maintenance.

technology.name: React, Next.js and TypeScript
technology.detail: A suitable option for component-based interfaces and sites that combine static content with server-rendered or interactive features. TypeScript helps describe application data and component contracts.

technology.name: CMS and database selection
technology.detail: An editorial CMS can manage pages and media; a relational database can support structured application data. We choose the combination around editing needs, relationships, permissions and operational ownership.

technology.name: APIs and release tooling
technology.detail: REST or GraphQL interfaces, automated checks, version control and environment-specific configuration support repeatable releases. Monitoring and recovery responsibilities are included in the operating plan when scoped.

deliverables: CMS models and editor guidance where included
Critical-journey test evidence and open-issue log
inputs: Approved designs or a separate design workstream, plus a prioritised feature list.
Content ownership, integration documentation and appropriate test accounts.
Hosting, domain and repository ownership, with an agreed launch decision-maker.
process: Define the architecture
Map routes, content, data, roles and integrations. Agree what counts as accepted behaviour.
Build in increments
Implement complete journeys and share working previews rather than disconnected screens.
Validate on staging
Review real content, permissions, accessibility, failures and device behaviour.
Release and hand over
Confirm configuration and recovery steps, launch with approval and transfer the operating documentation.
faq: Can your team maintain it after handover?
The handover includes the agreed source, setup and operating instructions. We can also define a separate maintenance arrangement for updates, monitoring and further development.
Can you reuse our current CMS or backend?
Often, yes. We first review its API, data quality, permissions and hosting constraints. Reuse or migration is chosen from that evidence rather than assumed at the start.
overview: Responsive websites, CMS models, APIs and access-controlled web applications.

title: Mobile app development
summary: iOS and Android applications for customer services, internal tools and digital products. We plan the core tasks, connect the backend and device features, and prepare tested builds for distribution.
useCases: Customers need a focused mobile experience beyond a responsive website.
A team needs field workflows with camera, location or intermittent connectivity.
An existing product needs a mobile companion connected to its backend.

work.title: Mobile flows and application structure
work.detail: We map navigation, onboarding, authentication and the main tasks before building screens. Platform conventions, touch interaction, safe areas, keyboard behaviour and permission requests are part of the interface rather than late additions.
work.check: Complete priority tasks on representative devices. Review small screens, long content, keyboard overlap, interrupted sessions and permission refusal.

work.title: Backend and device capabilities
work.detail: We connect documented APIs and define how the app handles synchronisation, cached data and failed requests. Features such as push notifications, media capture or location are included only where they support an agreed use case and have a clear consent flow.
work.check: Test weak connectivity, retry behaviour, expired credentials, duplicate actions and the agreed offline behaviour. Confirm sensitive values use appropriate platform storage rather than plain text preferences.

work.title: Testing and store preparation
work.detail: We prepare development and release configurations, signing requirements and test builds. Store descriptions, screenshots, permission explanations and account ownership are tracked as release dependencies. External review decisions remain with the platform.
work.check: Review installation, upgrades, navigation, crash reports and critical journeys on test distributions before preparing a submission build.

technology.name: React Native or Flutter
technology.detail: Cross-platform frameworks can share substantial application code across iOS and Android. The choice depends on required device features, animation needs, existing skills and long-term maintenance.

technology.name: Swift or Kotlin where appropriate
technology.detail: Platform-specific development or native modules may be appropriate for specialised device integration or platform behaviour. That requirement is assessed before committing to a shared-code approach.

technology.name: APIs, notifications and local data
technology.detail: The app needs explicit contracts with its backend, a token lifecycle and a plan for local state. Notifications, caching and synchronisation are designed around the product's actual data and connectivity needs.

inputs: Target platforms, priority journeys and any required device capabilities.
Backend documentation, test accounts and examples of real operating conditions.
Business-owned developer accounts, store assets and an approved data-handling policy.
process: Discover
Agree platforms, user tasks, device needs and backend dependencies.
Prototype
Validate navigation and important interactions before broad implementation.
Build and test
Deliver working journeys, integrate APIs and review on physical devices.
Prepare release
Complete acceptance testing and package the build and submission dependencies.
faq: Will the app work offline?
Offline behaviour must be designed explicitly. We agree which information is cached, which actions can be queued and how conflicts are resolved when connectivity returns.
Do you guarantee app-store approval?
No external approval can be guaranteed. We prepare the agreed technical and submission materials and identify platform requirements that affect the product.
overview: iOS and Android applications, device features and release preparation.

title: Graphic design & logo systems
summary: Logo systems and graphic assets for the places your business appears: websites, packaging, presentations, campaigns and print. We establish the visual rules, create the agreed applications and supply usable masters, exports and production guidance.
useCases: A new company needs a recognisable identity and a clear visual foundation.
A business has outgrown its current identity or accumulated inconsistent assets.
A team needs usable brand rules and templates for regular communication.

work.title: Foundation and creative direction
work.detail: We review your audience, offer, competitors and existing materials, then define the criteria the identity should meet. Naming or messaging can be included when specifically scoped. Concept directions are evaluated against business needs rather than personal preference alone.
work.check: Agree the audience, positioning and intended tone before selecting a direction. Record why the chosen direction fits the brief and where it must work.

work.title: Identity construction and applications
work.detail: We develop the mark, wordmark, variants, typography, palette and composition rules. Clear space, minimum sizes, monochrome use and image treatments are tested on representative digital and print applications.
work.check: Review small-size legibility, contrast, light and dark backgrounds, and the actual formats your team uses. Check that variants remain recognisable without relying on animation or colour.

work.title: Production files and team guidance
work.detail: We package editable masters and agreed exports with clear naming. Guidelines explain typography, colour references, spacing, asset choice and common mistakes. Templates make recurring tasks such as presentations or social posts easier to produce consistently.
work.check: Open exported assets, inspect their dimensions and colour settings, and have a team member apply the rules to a new example. Record third-party font and image licence responsibilities.

work.title: Graphic production and campaign applications
work.detail: Create the agreed presentation, social, packaging or print assets using a documented grid, type hierarchy and image treatment. Production specifications cover trim, bleed, resolution, colour references and required exports where relevant. Reusable templates include guidance for replacing copy and imagery without breaking the layout.
work.check: Review long and short content, inspect final exports and confirm production specifications and third-party font or image usage rights.

technology.name: Vector masters and SVG
technology.detail: Vector artwork supports scalable marks and precise production files. SVG suits many digital uses; PDF and raster variants cover other agreed applications. Exports are checked rather than simply generated in bulk.

technology.name: Digital and print colour references
technology.detail: Screen and print applications need appropriate colour definitions and practical proofs. We document the agreed RGB, hexadecimal and print references without assuming every device or printer reproduces colour identically.

technology.name: Editable templates and shared libraries
technology.detail: Templates can be prepared in the tools your team uses, such as Figma, presentation software or design applications. Shared styles and documented assets help keep future work consistent.

deliverables: Logo and wordmark variants with vector masters
Brand usage guide and asset register
inputs: Your company story, audiences, offer and existing brand materials.
A realistic list of digital and print applications where the identity must work.
A decision-maker, consolidated feedback and ownership information for supplied assets.
process: Define
Agree the business context, applications and creative criteria.
Explore
Develop and review distinct directions, then select one to refine.
Apply
Test the chosen identity on practical touchpoints and resolve weaknesses.
Package
Prepare the assets, templates and usage guidance for the team.
faq: Can this be a refresh rather than a complete rebrand?
Yes. We can preserve recognisable elements and address specific weaknesses, with the extent of the change agreed before exploration.
Does naming include trademark clearance?
Naming work, when included, can identify practical naming considerations. Formal trademark clearance and legal advice require an appropriate specialist.
overview: Logo systems, graphic assets, production files and reusable visual templates.

title: UI/UX & product design
summary: We work through how a product behaves before the development begins. User flows, interactive prototypes and component specifications cover the main tasks as well as errors, permissions and missing data.
useCases: A product has complicated workflows or users struggle to complete important tasks.
An early product needs its core journeys validated before development expands.
A growing application needs consistent components and an organised design system.

work.title: Research and journey definition
work.detail: We agree the research questions and available evidence, then map user roles, tasks, navigation and decision points. Interviews, existing analytics or usability sessions may inform the work where access and research scope are available.
work.check: Trace priority tasks from entry to completion. Identify missing decisions, unclear language, unnecessary steps and assumptions that still need evidence.

work.title: Prototype and interaction coverage
work.detail: Wireframes and linked prototypes explore flows before detailed visual refinement. Screen designs include validation, loading, empty results, success, errors and restricted access so engineering is not left to invent the difficult cases.
work.check: Observe representative users or stakeholders completing agreed tasks. Record findings and severity, then retest the changes that affect the core journey.

work.title: Components and engineering collaboration
work.detail: We organise reusable components, variants and tokens around the product's actual patterns. Behaviour notes cover focus, keyboard input, responsive changes and interaction dependencies. Engineering reviews help expose implementation constraints early.
work.check: Inspect consistency across journeys and confirm that states, assets and behaviour are documented. Resolve or explicitly record implementation questions before handover.

technology.name: Figma components and prototypes
technology.detail: Reusable variants and linked screens allow the team to review both appearance and task flow. File organisation, component naming and ownership are part of a usable design handover.

technology.name: Tokens and component specifications
technology.detail: Colour, type, spacing and interaction rules can map to CSS variables and coded components. We distinguish product-wide rules from one-off layouts to avoid an oversized, difficult-to-maintain library.

technology.name: Usability and accessibility review
technology.detail: Task-based evaluation can reveal problems that visual review misses. Focus order, labels, contrast and recovery paths are considered in design and checked again in the implemented product.

deliverables: Research questions, evidence summary and assumptions
Information architecture and priority user flows
Responsive screen designs and state inventory
Engineering handover and prioritised review findings
inputs: Product goals, user roles and the tasks that matter most.
Access to existing screens, support feedback and relevant product evidence.
Available research participants and an engineering contact for feasibility reviews.
process: Understand
Define user tasks, available evidence and success criteria.
Map
Agree information architecture and complete priority flows.
Prototype and evaluate
Test the interaction model and refine it before finalising screens.
Systemise
Document components, responsive rules and implementation decisions.
faq: Is this only a visual redesign?
No. The scope can address navigation, task flow, content and interaction behaviour as well as appearance. The work is prioritised around the product problem.
Can you work with our developers?
Yes. Regular feasibility reviews and component handover help connect design decisions with the existing frontend and backend architecture.
overview: User flows, interface states, prototypes and implementable component systems.

title: SaaS & custom software
summary: Customer portals, internal platforms and SaaS products built around your records, roles and operating process. We define the data model, permissions and integrations, then deliver working software with a release and maintenance plan.
useCases: Important work depends on disconnected spreadsheets and repetitive manual updates.
Customers or partners need a portal with controlled access to their information.
A business needs a focused product or internal platform that existing tools cannot support well.

work.title: Workflow and data modelling
work.detail: We map the current process, exceptions, roles and approval points. The data model defines records, relationships, ownership and validation rules. An incremental scope separates the essential workflow from later extensions.
work.check: Walk through realistic cases, including corrections and exceptions. Confirm who can create, view, change, approve and export each type of information.

work.title: Application and system integration
work.detail: We implement the interface, APIs and background tasks needed for complete workflows. Integrations with existing tools have documented contracts, retry rules and clear failure reporting. Imports and migrations are tested on representative data before a live cutover.
work.check: Test role boundaries, invalid data, duplicate requests, failed jobs and integration outages. Reconcile migrated records and confirm the agreed business rules with operators.

work.title: Operations and change management
work.detail: We define staging, production configuration, logging, backup responsibilities and deployment steps. Operator documentation explains routine tasks and recovery paths. Training and staged rollout can be included when the workflow affects multiple teams.
work.check: Complete user acceptance testing with the people doing the work. Confirm release ownership, rollback steps and how issues will be triaged after launch.

work.title: SaaS tenancy and product operations
work.detail: For multi-tenant products, define tenant boundaries, role permissions, onboarding, subscription states and administrative support workflows. Plan billing-provider events, audit records, account closure and data export around the product requirements. Tenant separation is enforced where data is accessed rather than relying on the interface to hide another customer’s records.
work.check: Test cross-tenant access, role changes, duplicate provider events, expired sessions and the account export or closure workflow included in scope.

technology.name: Web interfaces and typed APIs
technology.detail: React or Next.js with TypeScript can support dashboards and portals. API boundaries keep interface behaviour separate from business rules and make integration responsibilities easier to test.

technology.name: Relational data and background jobs
technology.detail: PostgreSQL or another suitable database can model structured records and relationships. Queues or scheduled jobs handle longer operations with explicit status, retries and duplicate-work protection.

technology.name: Identity, roles and observability
technology.detail: Authentication establishes identity; server-enforced authorisation determines access. Logs, error reporting and audit events are selected around the actions that operators need to understand and support.

deliverables: Workflow map, role matrix and prioritised backlog
Application source and working agreed workflows
Migration or import scripts where scoped
User acceptance findings and operator guidance
inputs: Process owners, sample records and examples of unusual or failed cases.
Existing system documentation, integration access and data ownership rules.
A product owner who can prioritise requirements and approve business behaviour.
process: Model the work
Agree users, data, rules and the first complete operational workflow.
Build a usable increment
Deliver a working slice that operators can review with realistic data.
Integrate and validate
Add dependencies, test permissions and rehearse imports or migration.
Roll out
Complete acceptance, train operators where scoped and transfer the operating runbook.
faq: Can you connect existing business systems?
We review their APIs, export formats, permissions and failure modes first. Integration scope depends on those capabilities and the quality of the available data.
Do we need to replace everything at once?
Usually a staged approach is possible. We identify a useful first workflow and define how it coexists with current systems before expanding.
overview: SaaS platforms, customer portals, internal tools and business-system integrations.

title: E-commerce stores & marketplaces
summary: Shopify and WooCommerce stores, plus Amazon marketplace setup and connected catalogue operations where included. We organise products, storefront content, checkout and fulfilment rules, then test the customer and order-management workflows before launch.
useCases: A business needs a new store with a manageable product catalogue.
An existing store needs clearer product information or a more coherent mobile journey.
A brand needs a custom storefront connected to an established commerce backend.

work.title: Catalogue and product experience
work.detail: We define product types, variants, collections, filtering and the information customers need before buying. Product pages account for imagery, availability, options, delivery information and relevant policies rather than treating every product as the same template.
work.check: Review representative products, unusual variants, missing media, sold-out states and mobile filters. Confirm that product data can be maintained by the store team.

work.title: Cart, checkout and integrations
work.detail: We connect the cart to the commerce platform and define quantity changes, discounts, availability errors and checkout handoff. Payment, shipping, tax and fulfilment configuration are reviewed with the business and relevant providers.
work.check: Use test orders to verify the cart, checkout, payment outcomes, confirmation and downstream order handling. Check rejected payments and changed availability as well as successful orders.

work.title: Migration and store operations
work.detail: Where required, we plan product and customer-data migration, URL mapping and redirects. Staff guidance covers catalogue updates, order management and third-party app dependencies. Release checks use an agreed set of products and ordering scenarios.
work.check: Reconcile imported records, check important URLs and verify that the team can manage products and recognise failed or incomplete orders.

work.title: Amazon listings and marketplace integration
work.detail: Prepare the agreed marketplace catalogue fields, identifiers, variants, imagery and listing content. Seller-account verification, brand permissions and product-category requirements are confirmed with the account owner. Where systems are connected, define how inventory, orders, returns and fulfilment status are reconciled between the storefront and marketplace.
work.check: Validate sample listings and variant relationships, test the scoped stock and order synchronisation, and record any marketplace approval or account dependency.

technology.name: Shopify themes or custom storefronts
technology.detail: A platform theme can support established editing and commerce workflows. A headless frontend is an option when its flexibility justifies the additional integration and maintenance responsibilities.

technology.name: Storefront APIs and hosted checkout
technology.detail: For a Shopify headless build, the Storefront Cart API manages cart state and provides a checkout URL. Customers complete checkout through the platform's checkout flow rather than a custom card-data form.

technology.name: Commerce integrations
technology.detail: Inventory, fulfilment, email and analytics connections need a defined source of truth and failure handling. Webhooks or scheduled synchronisation are chosen around the provider's capabilities and the required freshness.

technology.name: WooCommerce and WordPress operations
technology.detail: Assess theme and plugin compatibility, hosting, payments, shipping configuration and the content-editing workflow. Updates and backups need an operating owner; extensions are selected around requirements rather than installed without a dependency plan.

technology.name: Shopify, Amazon and catalogue connectors
technology.detail: Platform-supported integrations can connect eligible marketplace accounts and product records. Confirm supported regions, categories and account capabilities, then test mappings and exception handling before synchronising a full catalogue.

deliverables: Responsive storefront and agreed product templates
Migration and redirect plan where included
inputs: Product data, variants, imagery, inventory rules and ownership of the commerce account.
Approved shipping, returns and other purchase-related information.
Provider accounts and business approval for payment, delivery and fulfilment configuration.
process: Plan the store
Agree catalogue structure, purchase journeys and operational dependencies.
Design and build
Implement product discovery, templates and cart behaviour with real products.
Test orders
Verify checkout outcomes and the complete route from purchase to fulfilment.
Launch and transfer
Confirm configuration, migration and store-team readiness before release.
faq: Do we need a headless store?
Not necessarily. We compare editing needs, design requirements and maintenance responsibilities before recommending a platform theme or a separate frontend.
Can you move an existing store?
Migration can be included after reviewing data exports, product relationships, account constraints and URL history. It needs a rehearsal and a reconciliation plan.
overview: Shopify, WooCommerce and Amazon catalogue, checkout and order workflows.

title: 3D modelling & rendering
summary: Product models, architectural or brand visuals and rendered animation prepared for their intended use. We define geometry, materials, lighting and camera direction, then deliver the agreed stills, sequences or optimised real-time assets.
useCases: A website needs a distinctive interactive moment tied to its message.
A product or process is easier to explain through animation than static images.
A brand needs consistent motion rules across digital touchpoints.

work.title: Concept and motion direction
work.detail: We define the scene's purpose, storyboard, visual language and key states. A simple prototype tests the interaction before detailed production. Scroll and pointer inputs are mapped to meaningful transitions rather than decoration that competes with the content.
work.check: Review the message, pacing and relationship to the interface. Confirm that people can still read, navigate and use the page when animation is disabled.

work.title: Scene production and implementation
work.detail: We prepare geometry, materials, lighting, cameras and animation. Browser-based work can use custom shaders or particle systems where appropriate. Assets are optimised for the delivery format, with loading and resource cleanup considered during implementation.
work.check: Inspect transitions, scene bounds, resize behaviour and integration with the page. Confirm that animations reverse or reset correctly when navigation and scrolling change direction.

work.title: Performance and fallback behaviour
work.detail: We establish device-aware rendering limits and test representative desktop and mobile hardware. Resolution, particle count, textures and effects can adapt to the device. Reduced-motion and graphics-failure states retain the important content and actions.
work.check: Measure loading and interaction behaviour on the agreed device set. Check repeated navigation, context failure, hidden tabs, touch input and the static alternative.

work.title: Geometry, materials and rendering pipeline
work.detail: Agree real dimensions, level of detail and the use of CAD or other supplied source material. Prepare topology, UVs, material maps and lighting for the approved camera views. Real-time delivery adds explicit texture, geometry and loading limits; high-resolution still rendering follows a separate output specification.
work.check: Review silhouettes, scale, UV seams, material references and representative renders. For interactive assets, test file size, loading, appearance and performance on the target devices.

technology.name: Three.js and WebGL
technology.detail: A browser-based option for interactive scenes, cameras, materials and custom effects. The scene remains an enhancement around a usable HTML interface rather than the only way to access important information.

technology.name: Blender and glTF assets
technology.detail: 3D authoring can produce models and animation for web or rendered output. Mesh complexity, texture dimensions and export settings are selected for the target delivery and loading requirements.

technology.name: Scroll and animation systems
technology.detail: Animation timelines connect scene states with page position or user input. Rendering, resizing and cleanup need to cooperate with the website so fixed and pinned elements remain aligned.

deliverables: Agreed 3D assets or rendered animation files
inputs: The message the animation needs to communicate and where it will appear.
Brand files, product references, existing models and rights to supplied assets.
Target devices, delivery formats and the website or application integration constraints.
process: Define the moment
Agree the communication goal, key states and performance constraints.
Prototype
Test the scene and interaction with lightweight assets.
Produce
Develop the approved visuals, animation and interface integration.
Verify
Check pacing, scroll alignment, device performance and fallback behaviour.
faq: Will the same effects run on every phone?
Hardware and browser capabilities vary. We agree a representative device set and provide an adapted or static experience when the full scene is unsuitable.
Can you work with an existing website?
Yes, subject to its rendering, navigation and scroll architecture. We review those constraints before choosing an implementation approach.
overview: Product geometry, materials, lighting, rendered images and optimised 3D assets.

title: SEO & search content
summary: Technical SEO and search-focused content based on your actual website and customer questions. We investigate crawl and indexing issues, map intent to pages and prioritise improvements, with a record of the fixes and the search data used to assess them.
useCases: A website has crawl, indexing or content-structure problems.
A business needs landing pages and a measurement plan for a launch.
A team needs to understand which channels lead to useful enquiries.

work.title: Technical search and content structure
work.detail: We review important URLs, status codes, redirects, canonical tags, robots directives, sitemaps and internal links. Search intent is mapped to useful pages with distinct purposes. Content briefs identify audience questions and evidence needed from the business.
work.check: Recheck the agreed URLs after implementation. Validate redirects, indexability settings, metadata and links, while recognising that search engines control indexing and ranking decisions.

work.title: Landing pages and campaign preparation
work.detail: We connect the offer, audience, creative and destination page. Paid campaign work, when included, defines targeting, exclusions, creative variants and approval controls. The business authorises account access and campaign activation before publication.
work.check: Review the message, destination, form behaviour and campaign settings. Run a test enquiry through the complete journey before activating campaigns.

work.title: Measurement and iteration
work.detail: We define events, campaign naming and source information that can connect enquiries to useful business outcomes. Reports distinguish traffic, enquiries and qualified opportunities. Experiments record the hypothesis, observation window and decision criteria before results are interpreted.
work.check: Check missing or duplicate events and compare reports with actual enquiries. Report sample size, attribution gaps and data limitations alongside recommendations.

technology.name: Search Console and crawl tools
technology.detail: Search data and a crawl of the agreed URL set help identify technical problems and page opportunities. Findings are prioritised by evidence and implementation impact rather than a generic checklist alone.

technology.name: Analytics, events and tag management
technology.detail: Analytics or tag-management tools can measure agreed actions when configured for the site's data-handling choices. Events need consistent names and testing; an installed tracking script is not a complete measurement plan.

technology.name: CMS, landing pages and CRM connections
technology.detail: Content changes, campaign destinations and lead-source fields need to work together. CRM mapping can help separate an enquiry from a qualified lead when the business has a defined follow-up process.

inputs: Your offer, target markets, audiences and definition of a useful enquiry.
Appropriate access to the website, search data, analytics and campaign accounts.
Content reviewers and a clear lead follow-up process for interpreting results.
process: Establish a baseline
Review existing pages, available evidence and business outcomes.
Prioritise
Agree technical fixes, content opportunities and campaign dependencies.
Implement and validate
Publish approved changes and test the measurement journey.
Review
Explain observed results, limitations and the next prioritised actions.
faq: Can you guarantee rankings or a number of leads?
No. Search placement and campaign outcomes depend on external platforms, the market and the offer. We agree concrete deliverables and report evidence rather than promising a position or result.
Does this always include paid advertising?
No. Technical SEO, content structure, landing pages and paid campaign work can be scoped independently or combined where the business needs them.
overview: Crawl diagnostics, page-intent mapping, content improvements and search reporting.

title: AI services & intelligent automation
summary: Chatbots, AI-assisted workflows and bounded agents connected to your business information and tools. We also provide prompt-system design and AI consulting, with a defined use case, evaluation examples, permission boundaries and human-review requirements.
useCases: Information is repeatedly copied between forms, spreadsheets and business tools.
A team needs to classify, extract or summarise documents for human review.
People need an assistant that retrieves approved information or prepares actions in existing systems.

work.title: Workflow and data assessment
work.detail: We map the trigger, inputs, decision rules, systems and current manual steps. The review identifies which steps can be deterministic and which may benefit from a model. Data access, sensitive fields and the consequences of an incorrect result shape the design.
work.check: Agree representative examples, exception cases and acceptance criteria before implementation. Confirm that the required data can be used by the selected tools.

work.title: Automation and model integration
work.detail: APIs, webhooks or scheduled jobs connect the workflow. AI steps can retrieve approved documents, extract structured fields or prepare a tool action. Application code validates outputs and permissions; a model response is not treated as authorisation to change a business system.
work.check: Test malformed input, missing data, duplicate events, provider failures and attempts to trigger unauthorised actions. Require human approval for agreed consequential steps.

work.title: Evaluation and operation
work.detail: We create an evaluation set based on real tasks and define logging, retries, review queues and fallback behaviour. Changes to prompts, retrieval content or model configuration are checked against that baseline. Operators receive instructions for handling failures and correcting source information.
work.check: Review incorrect answers, unsupported claims and missed exceptions alongside successful examples. Verify that operators can identify a failed run and complete the task manually when needed.

work.title: Chatbots, knowledge retrieval and bounded agents
work.detail: Define supported questions and actions, the approved knowledge sources and escalation path. Retrieval includes document permissions and source references. An agent’s tool access is limited to authorised operations, with explicit confirmation for consequential actions, time and execution limits, and a useful failure or handover response.
work.check: Evaluate representative questions, missing knowledge, conflicting instructions, permission boundaries and failed tool calls. Confirm that uncertain or unsupported requests reach the agreed review path.

work.title: Prompt engineering, evaluation and AI consulting
work.detail: Review the proposed use case and establish a baseline before selecting a model or prompt pattern. Version the instructions, examples, output schema and evaluation dataset. Compare correctness, latency and operating requirements using realistic cases; consulting records whether an AI approach is justified and what controls would be needed for production.
work.check: Run repeatable evaluations against agreed examples, inspect invalid structured output and report limitations. Re-test material prompt, model or source-data changes before release.

technology.name: APIs, webhooks and workflow tools
technology.detail: Code or workflow platforms can move data and call existing services. Idempotency keys, bounded retries and visible run status help prevent repeated actions and silent failures.

technology.name: Model APIs and structured tool calls
technology.detail: Model-assisted steps can return structured data or request an application tool. Schema validation and server-side permission checks remain necessary; well-formed output does not establish that the information is correct.

technology.name: Retrieval and evaluation
technology.detail: Search over approved documents can supply relevant context to an assistant. Access controls, document freshness, source references and task-specific evaluations matter as much as the prompt itself.

deliverables: Workflow map and automation suitability assessment
Working agreed integrations or assistant features
inputs: A process owner, representative examples and a description of current manual work.
Authorised API access, approved source documents and data-handling requirements.
People who can review outputs and define which actions need explicit approval.
process: Assess
Choose a specific task and establish its data, risks and acceptance criteria.
Prototype
Test the approach against realistic examples before connecting live actions.
Integrate
Add validation, permissions, review controls and system connections.
Evaluate and operate
Review results against the baseline and hand over failure-handling and maintenance guidance.
faq: Does every automation need AI?
No. Fixed rules and standard integrations are often more predictable. We use a model-assisted step when the task benefits from language or unstructured-data handling.
Can an assistant act without human review?
Only within explicitly agreed permissions and workflow rules. Sensitive or consequential actions can be prepared for approval rather than executed automatically.
references: Structured tool calling and application execution
overview: Chatbots, agents, prompt systems, AI consulting and evaluated business workflows.

title: Cybersecurity & penetration testing
summary: Assess the security of agreed applications, APIs and infrastructure through an authorised, scoped engagement. Findings include reproducible evidence, business impact and remediation guidance, followed by a retest of the fixes included in the engagement.
useCases: An application needs an independent security review before release.
A business needs to understand its exposed services and access controls.
Engineering needs a prioritised remediation backlog rather than an unverified scanner export.

work.title: Rules of engagement
work.detail: Before testing, we agree the asset list, ownership, permitted techniques, test accounts, operating window and emergency contact. Third-party systems require the relevant permission. Production impact, evidence handling and stop conditions are documented; intrusive testing is never assumed to be part of a routine review.
work.check: Confirm written authorisation and scope boundaries. Validate test accounts and the incident contact before any active testing.

work.title: Application, API and configuration assessment
work.detail: Review authentication, session handling, role boundaries, object-level access, input processing and sensitive-data exposure. Configuration checks cover the agreed deployment surface. Manual investigation validates suspected vulnerabilities and connects weaknesses to realistic business workflows; an automated severity label alone does not establish exploitability or impact.
work.check: Record the affected asset, prerequisites, minimal reproducible evidence and impact. Remove false positives and avoid retaining unnecessary personal data.

work.title: Remediation and controlled retesting
work.detail: Provide engineering with actionable findings, affected locations, proposed controls and a prioritised remediation sequence. Retesting checks the agreed fixes and relevant regression paths. The final report distinguishes resolved, partially resolved and outstanding findings and states the scope and limitations of the assessment.
work.check: Reproduce each retested finding against the corrected build. Record evidence and exceptions without claiming the system is permanently secure.

technology.name: OWASP WSTG and API security checks
technology.detail: Use documented testing categories to plan coverage for web and API workflows. The applicable checks follow the agreed technology and threat model.

technology.name: Proxy, scanner and configuration tooling
technology.detail: Intercepting proxies and scoped scanners support manual investigation. Findings require validation; testing intensity and tooling access follow the written rules of engagement.

technology.name: Evidence and issue tracking
technology.detail: Restricted evidence storage and a remediation tracker connect each finding to its owner, fix, retest status and release. Retention and deletion are agreed in advance.

deliverables: Signed-off test scope and rules of engagement
inputs: Proof of authority over the named assets and permission for any third-party environment.
Architecture notes, relevant test accounts and a safe test environment where possible.
An engineering contact, escalation procedure and agreed evidence-retention requirements.
process: Authorise
Confirm asset ownership, exclusions, test windows and stop conditions.
Assess
Investigate the agreed attack surface and validate suspected weaknesses.
Remediate
Review findings with engineering and assign fixes by impact and dependency.
Retest
Check the included fixes and issue a report of the remaining exposure.
faq: Is this the same as an automated scan?
No. A scanner can identify candidate issues, but manual testing evaluates business logic, permissions and exploitability. Your scope will identify the systems and testing depth included.
Does the report certify compliance?
A penetration-test report records findings within a defined scope and period. Formal certification or regulated assurance is a separate engagement with the appropriate assessor and requirements.
overview: Authorised application testing, risk evidence, remediation guidance and retesting.

title: Cloud setup & IT support
summary: Cloud environments and workplace IT configured around the applications and people they support. The scope can cover AWS, Azure or Google Cloud foundations, migrations, identity, backups and operational support, with account ownership and escalation responsibilities documented.
useCases: A product needs a controlled path from a local build to production.
An organisation needs to consolidate access, devices or cloud accounts.
An existing environment lacks documented recovery and operational ownership.

work.title: Cloud foundations and access
work.detail: Map the application, data flows and operating requirements before selecting services. Separate environments, define network boundaries and establish role-based access. Business-owned accounts, multifactor authentication, service identities, logging and spending alerts form part of the foundation where the provider and scope support them.
work.check: Review access by role, verify environment separation and confirm that administration accounts remain under your ownership.

work.title: Migration, backup and recovery
work.detail: Inventory workloads and dependencies, plan data transfer and rehearse the cutover on a suitable environment. Specify backup frequency, retention, restore ownership and the acceptable recovery window. A completed backup job is not treated as proof that an application can be recovered.
work.check: Perform an agreed restore exercise, verify application data and record cutover, rollback and recovery steps.

work.title: IT support and operating procedures
work.detail: Define supported users, devices, applications, hours and escalation routes. Document onboarding, offboarding, access requests and common incidents. Support requests are triaged against agreed priorities; round-the-clock monitoring or guaranteed response times require an explicitly agreed operating arrangement.
work.check: Walk through representative access and incident requests. Confirm escalation contacts, audit records and the boundaries between provider support and your internal team.

technology.name: AWS, Azure or Google Cloud
technology.detail: Choose services around workload compatibility, region, identity and operational skills. Existing cloud commitments and data-location requirements influence the architecture.

technology.name: Infrastructure as code and deployment tooling
technology.detail: Repeatable configuration can use Terraform or provider-native templates. Changes are reviewed in version control, with environment values and sensitive credentials managed separately.

technology.name: Identity, monitoring and service management
technology.detail: Identity providers, alerting and ticketing tools make access changes and operational ownership traceable. Monitoring covers the agreed application dependencies as well as individual servers.

deliverables: Migration and rollback checklist where included
IT support procedures and escalation register
inputs: Business-owned provider accounts, approved administrators and application dependencies.
Existing infrastructure diagrams, data volumes and recovery requirements.
Supported locations, user and device inventory, operating hours and escalation contacts.
process: Inventory
Review accounts, workloads, devices and support responsibilities.
Design
Agree environments, identity, networking and recovery requirements.
Configure and rehearse
Provision services, validate access and test the migration or restore path.
Operate
Hand over runbooks and activate the agreed support process.
faq: Do we need to move to a different cloud?
Not necessarily. We first assess the environment you already use. Correcting permissions, backups or deployment practices can be more useful than moving providers.
Is continuous support included?
Setup and ongoing support are distinct scopes. Supported systems, service hours, response targets and maintenance responsibilities must be agreed before support begins.
overview: AWS, Azure or Google Cloud setup, migrations, recovery and IT operations.

title: Data analysis, science & dashboards
summary: Bring operational data into a form your team can question and use. We define metrics, prepare datasets and build analysis or dashboards; predictive modelling is included where the available data and decision justify it, with assumptions and validation recorded.
useCases: Different reports disagree on the same business metric.
A team manually combines exports to produce its regular reporting.
A forecasting or classification use case needs evaluation before production investment.

work.title: Source assessment and metric definitions
work.detail: Inventory source systems, identifiers, update frequency and access restrictions. Define what each metric measures, its reporting grain and the treatment of cancellations, missing values, time zones and late-arriving records. Establish a source of truth and a reconciliation sample before designing attractive charts.
work.check: Trace selected report values back to source records. Approve the metric dictionary and document unresolved gaps or inconsistent identifiers.

work.title: Data preparation, analysis and modelling
work.detail: Build reproducible extraction and transformation steps, inspect duplicates and outliers, and document exclusions. Exploratory analysis separates observed patterns from causal claims. Predictive work uses a baseline, an appropriate holdout or time-based validation, leakage checks and an error measure relevant to the intended business decision.
work.check: Re-run preparation from the agreed inputs. Check transformations and compare model results with the baseline and held-out data.

work.title: Dashboards and reporting operations
work.detail: Develop views around the decisions and user roles that matter. Specify filters, drill-through, permissions, refresh schedules and failure notifications. Charts include units, date ranges and clear definitions. Handover explains how new data enters the report and who investigates a failed refresh.
work.check: Reconcile key totals, test filters and permissions, and confirm refresh behaviour with the people responsible for using and maintaining the report.

technology.name: SQL and data pipelines
technology.detail: Use structured queries and versioned transformations to join records and calculate measures. The storage and orchestration approach follows data volume and update requirements.

technology.name: Python and statistical analysis
technology.detail: Pandas and suitable statistical or machine-learning tools support repeatable analysis. Method choice depends on sample quality, the target variable and the cost of errors.

technology.name: Power BI, Tableau or Looker Studio
technology.detail: Select a reporting tool around connectors, access control, sharing and existing licences. A custom application may suit more specialised operational workflows.

deliverables: Model evaluation and limitations where included
inputs: Authorised source access, sample extracts and an explanation of how records are created.
Decision questions, metric owners and examples of existing reports.
Reporting audiences, refresh needs, data-retention rules and available platform licences.
process: Define the decision
Agree the question, metric definitions and reporting audience.
Prepare the evidence
Inspect sources, reconcile samples and build repeatable transformations.
Analyse and present
Develop the scoped report or model and review it against real decisions.
Validate and maintain
Confirm totals, refresh operations, permissions and ownership.
faq: Can a dashboard fix unreliable source data?
It can expose inconsistencies, but it cannot manufacture missing records. We identify data-quality work and show where conclusions remain limited by the source.
Will a predictive model be accurate enough?
That is established through evaluation, not promised in advance. We compare with a baseline and report the errors and limitations that matter to your intended use.
overview: SQL reporting, data preparation, dashboards and evaluated predictive analysis.

title: No-code & workflow automation
summary: Connect the tools your business already uses, from a form submission through to a CRM update, document, notification or approval. Workflows include field mapping, duplicate protection and failure handling so the process remains understandable after handover.
useCases: Staff repeatedly copy the same information between business applications.
A lead or order needs consistent routing and follow-up.
An existing automation fails silently or creates duplicate records.

work.title: Process mapping and integration design
work.detail: Map the trigger, source of truth, required fields, branches and final system state. Separate actions that can run automatically from those needing approval. Check available connectors, API permissions, record volumes and application limits before deciding whether Zapier, Make, n8n or a custom integration is appropriate.
work.check: Approve field mappings, example payloads and expected outcomes for both standard and exception cases.

work.title: Workflow implementation and safeguards
work.detail: Implement filters, transformations, lookups and writes with clear names and reusable steps. Define idempotency or duplicate checks, retry limits, timeouts and what happens after a partial failure. Secrets stay in the platform credential store or another agreed secure mechanism, rather than in exported workflow files.
work.check: Test duplicate events, missing fields, expired credentials, unavailable destinations and a failure after an earlier action has already succeeded.

work.title: Monitoring, ownership and change control
work.detail: Provide a failure notification path, replay instructions and a record of external dependencies. Explain execution history, data retention and platform ownership. A named person owns credential renewal, connector changes and exceptions; workflow success is verified against the destination record, not simply a green execution indicator.
work.check: Run an end-to-end sample, inspect the destination and demonstrate how the owner identifies and recovers a failed execution.

technology.name: Zapier and Make
technology.detail: Managed connectors suit many common business workflows. Connector availability, task consumption and application capabilities are checked against the expected process volume.

technology.name: n8n and HTTP APIs
technology.detail: A suitable option for custom branching and API-heavy processes. Hosting, authentication, error workflows and execution-data retention need an operating plan.

technology.name: Webhooks, schemas and reconciliation
technology.detail: Defined payload schemas and event identifiers help validate incoming data. Reconciliation reports can identify records missed during an outage or credential failure.

inputs: Authorised access to the connected applications and realistic example records.
An explanation of approval rules, exceptions and the source of truth.
Expected event volumes, data sensitivity and an owner for ongoing credentials and failures.
process: Map
Document the process, exceptions and system responsibilities.
Connect
Configure credentials, payload mappings and required permissions.
Test
Exercise normal, duplicate and failure cases with representative data.
Hand over
Demonstrate monitoring, replay and routine workflow maintenance.
faq: Is no-code suitable for every integration?
No. Complex transactions, unsupported APIs or strict operational requirements may need custom software. We identify those constraints before choosing a platform.
Can you repair our existing workflows?
Yes. We inspect execution history, field mappings and application changes, then reproduce the failure and document the corrected behaviour and recovery process.
overview: Zapier, Make and n8n workflows with duplicate protection and recovery paths.

title: QA & software testing
summary: Test the journeys your users depend on, including permissions, interruptions and invalid input. We plan risk-based coverage, reproduce defects and build automated checks where they provide lasting value, with release findings your team can act on.
useCases: A product is approaching release without a clear acceptance checklist.
Regression defects recur after routine changes.
A team needs independent coverage across browsers, devices or user roles.

work.title: Test planning and environment readiness
work.detail: Agree the release scope, user roles, critical journeys and supported platforms. Identify integration boundaries, test data, environment dependencies and entry criteria. Coverage is prioritised by business impact and change risk; the plan states what will be tested manually, automated or excluded.
work.check: Confirm that test accounts, data resets, integration sandboxes and a stable build are available before the test cycle starts.

work.title: Functional, exploratory and automated testing
work.detail: Execute complete workflows, boundary cases and recovery paths. Investigate defects with reproducible steps, expected and actual results, environment details and supporting evidence. Automated browser and API checks target stable, high-value behaviour; screenshots and implementation details are not substitutes for meaningful assertions.
work.check: Re-run failures on the stated build, verify role and data assumptions, and distinguish a product defect from a test-environment failure.

work.title: Regression review and release reporting
work.detail: Retest fixes and check affected journeys for regressions. Report open defects by severity and impact, identify untested areas and record the release recommendation. Performance, accessibility and security checks can be included with their own scope; no finite test cycle proves the absence of all defects.
work.check: Review test evidence, remaining issues and exclusions with the release owner. Make the go-live decision and outstanding-risk ownership explicit.

technology.name: Playwright, Cypress or mobile test tooling
technology.detail: Select automation around the application platform, existing suite and release process. Keep test data and fixtures predictable enough to diagnose failures.

technology.name: API and integration checks
technology.detail: HTTP-level tests cover contracts, validation, authentication and failure responses. Third-party services are exercised through approved sandboxes or controlled substitutes.

technology.name: CI reporting and defect management
technology.detail: Versioned tests, build identifiers and issue records connect failures to the release under review. Unstable tests are investigated rather than silently retried indefinitely.

deliverables: Risk-based test plan and coverage matrix
Manual test results and reproducible defect reports
Release report with exclusions and open issues
inputs: A release candidate, prioritised requirements and agreed acceptance criteria.
Representative test accounts, devices and data with appropriate usage permission.
A defect owner, release schedule and access to approved integration test environments.
process: Plan coverage
Agree risks, supported platforms and the release acceptance criteria.
Prepare
Establish the test environment, accounts, data and build identifiers.
Execute and investigate
Run the planned coverage and document reproducible defects.
Retest and report
Verify fixes and present remaining release risks to the decision-maker.
faq: Will you automate every test?
No. Automation is most useful for repeatable, valuable checks. Exploratory testing and human review remain important for unfamiliar behaviour, visual judgement and changing requirements.
Can testing run alongside development?
Yes. Coverage can be reviewed incrementally, with stable checks added to the delivery pipeline. Release-specific validation still needs an agreed build and environment.
overview: Risk-based functional, browser, device and API testing with release evidence.

title: Social media management
summary: A managed publishing and community workflow for the social channels your customers use. We plan content around your offer, prepare channel-specific assets and copy, organise approvals and report on meaningful audience actions rather than posting volume alone.
useCases: Publishing depends on last-minute requests with no clear content owner.
Your channels need a consistent voice and repeatable production schedule.
Comments and messages need a defined response and escalation process.

work.title: Channel audit and editorial plan
work.detail: Review profile setup, existing content, audience behaviour and the business actions each channel should support. Establish content themes, formats and a publishing cadence your team can sustain. The calendar specifies the purpose, asset requirements, source material and approval owner for each post.
work.check: Approve channel roles, content themes and the first calendar. Check profile information, links and access permissions.

work.title: Production, approvals and publishing
work.detail: Create or adapt the agreed assets, write platform-specific copy and prepare captions, accessibility text and tracked destinations where supported. Separate creative approval from scheduling. Changes to offers, claims or product availability are checked with the relevant business owner before a post goes live.
work.check: Preview crops and text on the intended channel, verify destinations and retain the approved version in the publishing record.

work.title: Community handling and review
work.detail: Define responses for routine questions and routes for complaints, sensitive information and sales enquiries. Report performance in the context of content purpose and available platform data. Recommendations distinguish engagement, website actions and qualified demand rather than treating every interaction as equivalent.
work.check: Sample response handling and escalation records. Review which content led to useful actions and identify the next editorial changes.

technology.name: Native channel tools and schedulers
technology.detail: Use business-owned profiles and approved publishing permissions. Scheduling tools are selected around the supported formats, approval workflow and reporting requirements.

technology.name: Content libraries and production templates
technology.detail: Maintain reusable formats, asset naming and source links so recurring posts can be produced without losing track of approval or usage rights.

technology.name: Platform analytics and tracked links
technology.detail: Combine available channel metrics with consistent UTM tagging. Attribution limits, unavailable data and differences between platform definitions remain visible in reporting.

deliverables: Approved post copy and scoped creative assets
inputs: Business-owned channel access, brand assets and approved account administrators.
Product information, offer dates, source material and image or video usage rights.
A content approver, response guidelines and contacts for complaints or sales enquiries.
process: Audit
Review accounts, audience behaviour and the purpose of each channel.
Plan
Agree formats, content themes, production responsibilities and approvals.
Publish
Prepare, review and schedule the approved content.
Review
Assess audience actions, community issues and the next content priorities.
faq: Does management include filming and photography?
Production requirements are stated in the scope. We can work with supplied assets or connect photography, video and design services where new material is needed.
Do you guarantee follower growth?
No. We agree the activities and reporting measures, but audience response depends on the offer, content, distribution and platform behaviour. Purchased engagement is not part of the service.
overview: Editorial calendars, channel-specific production, publishing and community handling.

title: Paid advertising
summary: Paid campaigns built around a defined offer, a suitable landing experience and measurable conversion events. We organise account structure, targeting, creative tests and reporting so your team can distinguish traffic from leads and sales.
useCases: An offer needs a controlled acquisition test before a wider rollout.
Existing campaigns generate clicks without clear lead quality or attribution.
Advertising accounts need a cleaner structure and accountable change history.

work.title: Account and measurement setup
work.detail: Review business-owned ad accounts, access roles, conversion definitions and landing pages. Specify event naming, consent-dependent tracking and CRM handoff. Select search, audience or video campaigns according to buying intent and the offer; additional channels are not added merely to increase activity.
work.check: Test a sample conversion through the agreed reporting path. Check duplicate events, destination URLs, campaign limits and account permissions.

work.title: Campaign structure and creative testing
work.detail: Build the agreed campaigns, keyword or audience groups, exclusions and placement settings. Prepare a documented test plan for messages, visuals and landing-page variants. Creative claims, destinations and campaign settings require business approval before activation, and platform review remains outside our control.
work.check: Review targeting, copy, creative formats and tracking against the launch checklist. Record each experiment and its decision criteria.

work.title: Optimisation and commercial reporting
work.detail: Monitor search terms, placements, delivery and conversion quality. Investigate changes in results alongside tracking failures, sales follow-up and landing-page behaviour. Reports distinguish platform-reported conversions from CRM outcomes and state attribution windows, sample limitations and recommended next actions.
work.check: Reconcile a sample of reported leads with CRM records. Review spend against the authorised limits and obtain approval for material changes.

technology.name: Google Ads, Meta Ads Manager and TikTok Ads
technology.detail: Campaign types and targeting follow the offer and customer journey. Account ownership, billing access and advertising permissions remain with your business.

technology.name: Analytics and conversion instrumentation
technology.detail: Tag management, platform events and approved server-side integrations can support measurement. Configuration follows consent requirements and must be validated against actual submissions or orders.

technology.name: CRM and experiment reporting
technology.detail: Connect campaign source information with lead stages where the CRM supports it. A change log records hypotheses, creative variants and the context of observed results.

deliverables: Approved ad copy and scoped creative variants
Performance report linked to agreed business outcomes
inputs: Authorised advertising accounts, spending limits and approval responsibilities.
An approved offer, landing pages, product claims and creative usage rights.
Analytics and CRM access where included, plus a definition of a qualified lead or sale.
process: Audit and plan
Review the offer, account history and conversion measurement.
Build and approve
Prepare campaigns, creative variants and launch settings.
Launch and validate
Activate approved campaigns and verify tracking and destinations.
Optimise
Review qualified outcomes and adjust the agreed variables.
faq: Is advertising spend included in the service?
Media spend is paid through your own advertising accounts. The engagement specifies management activities and who may authorise changes to campaign limits.
Can you guarantee a return on ad spend?
No. Results depend on demand, the offer, competition, creative, conversion experience and sales follow-up. We agree how the test will be measured and report the evidence and limitations.
overview: Google, Meta and TikTok campaign setup, creative tests and conversion tracking.

title: Email marketing
summary: Email programmes for the stages that matter: welcoming a subscriber, supporting a purchase, retaining a customer or re-engaging an opted-in audience. We build segments, templates and automations with tested links, clear consent records and useful reporting.
useCases: Customer emails are sent manually without consistent segmentation.
An online store needs welcome, post-purchase or re-engagement sequences.
Existing campaigns have unclear consent, unreliable tracking or poor template behaviour.

work.title: Audience, consent and sending setup
work.detail: Review how contacts are collected, the permission recorded and the events available for segmentation. Define suppression rules, unsubscribe handling and ownership of the sending domain. Work with the authorised administrator on SPF, DKIM and DMARC configuration where included; list provenance is checked before importing contacts.
work.check: Verify consent fields, suppression behaviour and a test unsubscribe. Confirm the sending configuration and administrator ownership.

work.title: Templates, copy and lifecycle automation
work.detail: Design responsive templates and write messages for an agreed customer stage and action. Configure entry criteria, delays, branches, exits and frequency rules. Personalisation includes sensible fallbacks, and purchase or support events prevent contacts from continuing through an unsuitable sequence.
work.check: Review test messages across representative clients. Exercise segment entry, fallback content, sequence exits and all destination links.

work.title: Sending, quality review and reporting
work.detail: Use test segments and staged activation where appropriate. Monitor delivery signals, bounces, complaints, unsubscribes and downstream actions. Reports explain the limits of open-rate measurement and focus on clicks, relevant customer events and outcomes that the connected systems can substantiate.
work.check: Check campaign audiences and exclusions before sending. Review errors, complaints and conversion events after activation and log adjustments.

technology.name: Klaviyo, Mailchimp, HubSpot or similar platforms
technology.detail: Choose the platform around your commerce or CRM integration, event model, audience size and account ownership. Existing systems are assessed before proposing a migration.

technology.name: HTML email and reusable templates
technology.detail: Responsive structures, accessible text, fallback styling and image handling are tested for the agreed email-client coverage rather than assumed from a browser preview.

technology.name: DNS and event integrations
technology.detail: Authenticated sending and reliable customer events support delivery and segmentation. Credentials, event mappings and contact-retention rules are documented.

deliverables: Reusable email templates and approved copy
Client, link and workflow test results
inputs: An authorised email account and evidence of contact collection and permissions.
Brand assets, approved offers and access to the relevant CRM or commerce events.
A sending-domain administrator, campaign approver and agreed audience-exclusion rules.
process: Assess
Review contact provenance, sending setup and available customer events.
Design
Agree segments, messaging and lifecycle entry and exit conditions.
Test and activate
Validate templates and complete journeys before approved activation.
Review
Monitor delivery quality and customer actions, then adjust the programme.
faq: Can you send to a purchased mailing list?
We build programmes around documented permission and applicable sending requirements. A supplied address list must be assessed for provenance and permitted use before any import or campaign.
Can you use our existing templates?
Yes. We inspect their mobile behaviour, structure and editing workflow, then agree whether refinement or replacement is the better use of the project scope.
overview: Audience segments, responsive templates, lifecycle sequences and delivery checks.

title: Influencer & affiliate marketing
summary: Partnership programmes with a clear brief, agreed usage rights and a traceable path from placement to outcome. We support creator selection, outreach preparation, campaign coordination and affiliate tracking, with approvals and commercial terms recorded before activation.
useCases: A launch needs relevant creators rather than a large, unqualified contact list.
Affiliate activity needs consistent links, codes and reconciliation.
Your team needs a repeatable process for partner briefs, approvals and reporting.

work.title: Partner research and programme design
work.detail: Define audience fit, geography, content standards and the role a partner should play. Review publicly available audience and engagement signals without treating follower totals as proof of influence. Document eligibility, offer structure, exclusions and the intended measurement approach before preparing a shortlist.
work.check: Review the selection rationale, audience evidence and conflicts. Approve a shortlist and programme criteria before outreach.

work.title: Briefs, rights and campaign coordination
work.detail: Prepare the creative brief, deliverables, posting requirements, disclosure responsibilities and review points. Record the permitted channels, duration and territory for reuse of supplied content. Coordinate approved outreach and logistics; creator agreements and negotiated commercial commitments require the designated business approver.
work.check: Confirm each partner has an approved brief, delivery dates, usage permissions and a clear contact for questions or revisions.

work.title: Tracking and outcome reconciliation
work.detail: Assign consistent partner identifiers, links or codes and test their destinations. Define attribution windows and how returns, cancellations, duplicate orders and code leakage affect reporting. Separate content delivery, attributed activity and confirmed commercial outcomes rather than treating all tracked clicks as sales.
work.check: Test links and codes, reconcile a sample against order or CRM records and document any attribution or data-access limitations.

technology.name: Creator research and assessment tools
technology.detail: Public profiles and authorised research platforms support shortlist preparation. Audience quality and relevance need contextual review rather than a single numerical score.

technology.name: Affiliate platforms and campaign identifiers
technology.detail: Use the platform supported by your storefront or CRM. Partner identifiers, codes and tracking parameters must remain consistent through the customer journey.

technology.name: Rights and deliverable registers
technology.detail: A shared record connects approved briefs, contracts, assets, publication evidence and reporting. Sensitive partner information is restricted to the people who need it.

deliverables: Tested tracking links or code specification
inputs: Product information, target audiences and partner-selection restrictions.
An authorised approver for agreements, offers, content claims and creator commitments.
Storefront or CRM tracking access and clear rules for permitted content reuse.
process: Define
Agree the audience, programme rules and intended outcomes.
Select
Research and review potential partners against the criteria.
Coordinate
Issue approved briefs and manage deliverables and review points.
Measure
Validate tracking and reconcile attributed outcomes.
faq: Do you guarantee a creator will participate?
No. Participation and terms depend on the creator and the proposed collaboration. We manage the agreed research and coordination work and record each partner status.
