Can creator content be used in paid advertising?
Only where the necessary permissions and platform access have been agreed. Organic publication does not automatically grant advertising, editing or unrestricted reuse rights.
overview: Partner research, creator briefs, usage rights and attributable campaign records.

title: Content marketing & campaign copy
summary: Content organised around customer questions and the decisions they need to make. We plan topics, prepare evidence-led briefs and produce the agreed articles, landing pages or campaign copy, with subject review and distribution responsibilities built into the process.
useCases: Your website has activity and articles but no clear editorial direction.
A complex offer needs explanations for different customer stages.
Sales and marketing need consistent messages and reusable campaign material.

work.title: Audience questions and editorial architecture
work.detail: Review the offer, customer objections, existing pages and available subject expertise. Map topics to buying stages and existing destinations, separating acquisition content from product education and sales support. The plan identifies where original interviews, examples or data are needed rather than filling every topic with interchangeable claims.
work.check: Approve the audience, purpose, destination and evidence requirements for priority pieces. Check for duplicated topics and unsupported product statements.

work.title: Briefing, drafting and subject review
work.detail: Prepare outlines, source notes and the intended reader action before drafting. Write to the required format, with concrete examples, useful headings and a consistent voice. Subject experts review factual statements and any regulated claims; editorial revisions resolve unclear explanations without inventing results, customers or statistics.
work.check: Check each draft against the brief, verify sources and obtain the relevant factual and brand approvals before publication.

work.title: Publishing, distribution and measurement
work.detail: Prepare metadata, internal links, image requirements and channel adaptations. Agree who publishes and distributes each asset, then track suitable signals such as relevant visits, content-assisted enquiries or sales-team use. Review content as an editorial portfolio, accounting for its purpose and maturity.
work.check: Verify the published page, links and tracking. Record distribution activity and distinguish observed results from unsupported attribution claims.

technology.name: Editorial calendars and content inventories
technology.detail: Track audience, topic, owner, status, evidence and destination. A shared inventory makes revision and repurposing easier than managing disconnected files.

technology.name: CMS and content optimisation tooling
technology.detail: Use the existing publishing system where practical. Heading structure, page relationships, metadata and image requirements are prepared alongside the copy.

technology.name: Analytics and CRM context
technology.detail: Connect measurable customer actions with content destinations where reliable data exists. Reporting acknowledges attribution gaps and the role of other sales touchpoints.

inputs: Product information, customer questions and access to relevant subject experts.
Existing content, brand voice guidance and permission to use supplied examples.
A factual approver, publishing owner and the reporting data available to the project.
process: Map
Review the offer, audience questions and existing content.
Brief
Define each asset, its evidence and intended reader action.
Write and review
Draft, fact-check and revise with the subject owner.
Publish and assess
Check publication and review the agreed distribution and response signals.
faq: How is this different from standalone copywriting?
This service includes the editorial programme: topic selection, asset relationships, distribution and review. Standalone writing can focus on an individual page, article or manuscript.
Can you write about specialist subjects?
Yes, when the project provides access to reliable source material and a suitable subject reviewer. Unverified claims are raised as questions rather than presented as established facts.
overview: Editorial programmes, evidence-led briefs, landing pages and campaign copy.

title: Lead generation & sales outreach
summary: A prospecting process built around who your service genuinely fits, with researched account criteria, relevant messages and a CRM handoff. Outreach channels and contact use are reviewed for the intended market before any campaign is activated.
useCases: Sales activity relies on broad lists with little account qualification.
Enquiries and outbound conversations are lost between tools or team members.
A business needs a controlled test of a specific market and offer.

work.title: Ideal-customer criteria and account research
work.detail: Define company attributes, buying roles, likely needs and disqualifying conditions. Build a researched account list from permitted sources and record why each account fits. Contact data provenance, permitted use, retention and market-specific outreach requirements are part of planning rather than an afterthought.
work.check: Sample the list for relevance, duplicate accounts and source quality. Approve the target criteria and contact-use approach before outreach.

work.title: Messaging and controlled outreach setup
work.detail: Write messages around a substantiated reason to contact the prospect and one appropriate next step. Configure authorised channels, suppression rules, opt-out handling and stopping conditions. Sending identity, account access and any automated sequence require approval; replies and objections are routed to an accountable person.
work.check: Review messages and sender configuration, test opt-out handling and confirm that a reply or negative response stops the relevant sequence.

work.title: Qualification, CRM handoff and review
work.detail: Define the difference between a researched account, a reply, a booked meeting and a qualified opportunity. Map ownership, source information, next actions and follow-up deadlines into the CRM. Report list quality and conversation outcomes without labelling every contact as a sales-ready lead.
work.check: Trace sample conversations into the CRM, check suppression synchronisation and review the agreed qualification evidence and follow-up ownership.

technology.name: Research sources and data validation
technology.detail: Use sources and enrichment tools permitted for the intended activity. Validation reduces obvious errors but does not establish consent or guarantee that a person is interested.

technology.name: CRM and sequence tooling
technology.detail: Configure account records, conversation stages and responsible owners. Automated steps are constrained by approved rules and stop conditions.

technology.name: Sending and suppression controls
technology.detail: Approved channels, sender authentication and shared suppression records support controlled operations. Unsubscribe and objection handling must be maintained throughout the programme.

deliverables: Researched account list with source fields
CRM fields, stages and handoff rules
inputs: A clear offer, target markets and evidence for claims made in outreach.
Approved contact sources, channel permissions and the applicable contact-use requirements.
CRM ownership, qualification rules and someone responsible for responding to conversations.
process: Define fit
Agree the market, buying roles and disqualification criteria.
Research
Build and validate a sample list using permitted sources.
Approve and test
Review messaging, channel rules and suppression behaviour.
Handoff and learn
Track conversations and improve the process using qualified outcomes.
faq: Do you guarantee meetings or sales?
No. We specify the research, setup, outreach and reporting work. Prospect response and purchasing decisions depend on fit, timing, the offer and your sales process.
Will you send messages without approval?
No. Targeting, messages, channels and operating rules are approved before activation. Contact data must be suitable for the intended use and market.
overview: Prospect research, approved outreach, qualification rules and CRM handoffs.

title: Brand strategy & positioning
summary: Clarify who your business serves, the problem it addresses and the reasons a customer should choose it. The output is a usable positioning and messaging framework that guides your identity, website, campaigns and sales material.
useCases: Your offer is described differently by sales, marketing and leadership.
A business is entering a new market or serving a more specific audience.
An identity refresh needs a strategic brief beyond visual preferences.

work.title: Business, audience and competitive evidence
work.detail: Review the offer, existing customer feedback, commercial priorities and competing alternatives. Interviews or research are included where scoped. Separate internal beliefs from evidence and identify the customer needs, objections and decision criteria that the brand must address. Findings state where further research is still needed.
work.check: Review the evidence sources and agree the priority audience and business problem before developing positioning options.

work.title: Positioning and value proposition
work.detail: Develop the category context, intended audience, primary benefit and credible reasons to believe. Assess possible positioning routes against the business offer and available proof. Product claims, credentials and customer results are only used where substantiated; a desired future capability is distinguished from a current one.
work.check: Test the proposition against realistic customer questions and competitive alternatives. Select and approve a direction with a documented rationale.

work.title: Messaging and practical application
work.detail: Translate the strategy into a message hierarchy, tone principles, short descriptions and channel examples. Show how the proposition changes in emphasis for a homepage, service explanation, presentation or campaign without contradicting itself. Provide a creative brief for subsequent identity and design work.
work.check: Have the relevant team apply the framework to a new communication. Resolve ambiguous terminology and confirm who approves future claims or revisions.

technology.name: Research and interview frameworks
technology.detail: Structured discussion guides and evidence notes keep the strategy grounded in what customers and the business can substantiate.

technology.name: Positioning and message architecture
technology.detail: A clear hierarchy connects the proposition, supporting arguments and proof. Frameworks are used to make decisions, not as decorative workshop outputs.

technology.name: Brand and content systems
technology.detail: Approved terminology, tone rules and application examples can be incorporated into design libraries, editorial guidance and sales templates.

deliverables: Creative brief and channel application examples
inputs: Business objectives, current services and an accurate account of existing capabilities.
Customer feedback, research or access to agreed interview participants.
Leadership availability, claim evidence and a decision-maker for the positioning direction.
process: Discover
Review the business, audience evidence and competing alternatives.
Choose a position
Develop and evaluate strategic routes against the offer and proof.
Build the message
Define the proposition, supporting arguments and tone.
Apply
Test the framework on actual sales and marketing communications.
faq: Does strategy include a new logo?
The strategic framework and creative brief guide identity work. Logo design and the production identity system can be connected as a separate workstream.
Can this work for a new company without customer data?
Yes. We document assumptions explicitly and use the evidence available. Research or market testing can then address the decisions carrying the greatest uncertainty.
overview: Audience definition, positioning, value propositions and message architecture.

title: Video marketing & UGC advertising
summary: Short-form video built for a specific offer, audience and placement. We develop hooks, scripts and production briefs, then prepare the agreed edits and variants for organic channels or paid advertising, with usage rights and tracking destinations defined.
useCases: An offer needs video concepts that explain the benefit quickly.
Existing footage needs channel-specific cuts and stronger opening sequences.
A campaign needs a controlled set of creative variants for testing.

work.title: Audience, placement and creative brief
work.detail: Agree the customer stage, offer, placement, primary action and claims the video can support. Develop concepts with a clear opening, message sequence and ending. Creator-led or UGC-style content is planned around truthful product use; a scripted performance is not presented as an independent customer testimonial.
work.check: Approve the script, claims, reference direction and production responsibilities before recording or editing begins.

work.title: Production coordination and variant editing
work.detail: Prepare shot lists, creator instructions and asset requirements. Edit the supplied or commissioned footage into the agreed durations and aspect ratios, with captions, sound treatment and graphics. Track which variable changes in each variant so a creative test has a usable hypothesis.
work.check: Review legibility, safe areas, caption accuracy and audio on the intended placements. Confirm rights for people, music, footage and advertising reuse.

work.title: Delivery and campaign feedback
work.detail: Package exports and a variant register with filenames tied to the concept, hook and placement. Coordinate with the campaign owner on landing destinations and test results. Recommendations consider delivery and audience response alongside creative execution; a strong-looking edit does not by itself establish sales impact.
work.check: Check exported files, platform previews and variant naming. Review the agreed campaign signals before selecting the next concepts or revisions.

technology.name: Script, storyboard and shot-list workflows
technology.detail: Plan the opening, supporting evidence and call to action before production. A shared brief keeps the editor, creator and campaign manager aligned.

technology.name: Editing, captions and motion graphics
technology.detail: Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, After Effects or appropriate equivalents support editing and graphics. Delivery specifications follow the placement rather than one universal export.

technology.name: Creative testing and asset tracking
technology.detail: Maintain a record of hooks, edits and approved uses. Campaign data can inform creative decisions where the account owner provides reliable placement and outcome reporting.

deliverables: Creator or production instructions where included
Agreed video edits and test variants
Asset-rights register and creative review notes
inputs: An approved offer, substantiated product claims and target placements.
Source footage or agreed production access, with participant and asset permissions.
Brand assets, creator agreements where relevant and a designated campaign approver.
process: Brief
Agree the audience, offer, placement and permissible claims.
Script
Develop hooks, concepts and production requirements.
Produce and edit
Record or assemble footage and prepare the approved variants.
Deliver and review
Check exports and use campaign evidence to guide subsequent edits.
faq: Does UGC mean you will invent customer reviews?
No. Genuine customer material requires permission and an accurate account of their experience. Creator-led advertising can use a scripted demonstration with the appropriate disclosures.
Can you work with footage we already have?
Yes. We review its technical quality, coverage and usage rights, then agree which concepts and formats can be produced from that material.
overview: Short-form concepts, UGC-style production briefs and testable ad variants.

title: Video editing & animation
summary: Turn recorded material and a clear brief into a finished story. We handle the agreed edit, motion graphics, colour and sound finishing, then prepare exports for the actual channels, screen formats and accessibility requirements of the project.
useCases: Raw footage needs an editorial structure and a consistent visual finish.
A product or process is easier to explain through animation.
A finished film needs cut-downs, captions and alternate screen formats.

work.title: Editorial structure and asset preparation
work.detail: Review the source footage, audio, script and intended audience. Organise media, identify missing coverage and agree the running time and story structure. A rough cut establishes the sequence and message before detailed animation or finishing, preventing late structural changes from consuming production work.
work.check: Check media availability, frame rates, audio synchronisation and the approved edit outline. Agree what can be achieved from the supplied footage.

work.title: Editing and motion design
work.detail: Develop the edit, pacing, titles and scoped animated sequences. Motion graphics follow a storyboard or approved reference direction, including timing, transitions and required text. Version reviews use a common timecoded reference so comments can be consolidated and resolved without conflicting instructions.
work.check: Approve the picture sequence and animation direction before final finishing. Check factual text, continuity, graphics and the intended message.

work.title: Finishing, accessibility and exports
work.detail: Apply the agreed colour treatment, audio cleanup and mix, captions and end cards. Prepare aspect ratios, codecs and delivery files for the specified channels. Project-file handover, source collection and archive retention are agreed explicitly, alongside music, footage, font and voice usage permissions.
work.check: Review the final export from beginning to end, check captions and audio, and verify dimensions, duration and compatibility with the delivery specification.

technology.name: Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve and editing workflows
technology.detail: Choose the editing environment around source formats, collaboration and handover needs. Proxy media can support review of high-resolution footage on practical hardware.

technology.name: After Effects and motion graphics
technology.detail: Use reusable graphic components and organised compositions for scoped 2D animation. Complex 3D assets or character animation require an explicitly defined production scope.

technology.name: Colour, sound and caption delivery
technology.detail: Finishing uses the agreed colour pipeline, audio requirements and subtitle formats. Social, web and broadcast outputs need different checks and exports.

deliverables: Rough cut and consolidated review version
Export specification and project handover where included
inputs: Source footage, audio and scripts, with information about recording formats.
Brand assets, the intended channels and permissions for all supplied material.
An approver able to consolidate timecoded comments and confirm the final sequence.
process: Prepare
Review the media and agree the editorial plan and delivery formats.
Edit
Build the rough cut and resolve the sequence before finishing.
Animate and finish
Produce approved graphics, colour, sound and captions.
Deliver
Check master files, alternate versions and the agreed archive package.
faq: Can you repair badly recorded footage or audio?
We assess the source before committing to a result. Some issues can be improved; missing detail, clipped audio or unusable coverage may need replacement material.
Will we receive editable project files?
That is agreed in the scope. The handover also needs to identify linked media, plugins, fonts and third-party assets whose licences cannot automatically be transferred.
overview: Editorial cuts, motion graphics, colour, sound, captions and delivery exports.

title: Voiceover & podcast editing
summary: Clear, consistent spoken audio for podcasts, explainers and brand communication. The service can include script preparation, voice-session coordination, dialogue editing, cleanup and episode assembly, with the intended use and delivery format agreed before production.
useCases: Podcast recordings need editing, consistent levels and a repeatable release workflow.
A video or product explanation needs timed narration.
Remote interviews need dialogue assembly and correction of recording inconsistencies.

work.title: Script, session and voice requirements
work.detail: Review the script, pronunciation, intended audience and tone. Confirm voice selection, language, recording setup and usage rights, including channels and duration. Narration timing is checked against the picture or script; podcast work establishes the episode structure, intro, outro and editorial boundaries.
work.check: Approve the script and pronunciation guide, confirm participant permissions and check a recording sample before the full session.

work.title: Dialogue editing and episode assembly
work.detail: Select and arrange takes, remove agreed errors and distracting repetitions, and align dialogue with picture where relevant. Noise reduction, de-clicking and level correction are applied with care to avoid unnatural speech. Editorial changes preserve the speaker’s meaning and are flagged where context is ambiguous.
work.check: Review speech continuity, timing and intelligibility. Confirm that cuts have not changed the meaning of an interview or removed necessary context.

work.title: Mixing, masters and release materials
work.detail: Balance voices, music and transitions against the agreed listening environment and delivery requirements. Prepare masters, distribution files and scoped show notes or transcripts. Keep a version record linking the approved edit to its released files and document any audio or music licensing restrictions.
work.check: Listen to the complete master on representative playback devices, check channel layout and loudness requirements, and inspect the final file metadata.

technology.name: Audition, Reaper, Pro Tools or equivalent DAWs
technology.detail: Session organisation, non-destructive editing and versioned renders make dialogue changes traceable. The choice follows recording formats and collaboration requirements.

technology.name: Dialogue restoration and processing
technology.detail: Appropriate equalisation, dynamics and noise reduction can improve a usable recording. Processing cannot reliably recover speech that was never captured or is heavily clipped.

technology.name: Podcast and narration delivery formats
technology.detail: Exports follow the destination platform or video workflow. Sample rate, bit depth, channel layout and loudness targets are confirmed rather than assumed.

deliverables: Assembled and mixed episode or narration
inputs: Source recordings or an agreed recording session and voice-selection process.
Scripts, pronunciation notes, brand tone and music or participant permissions.
The delivery platform, required duration and an approver for editorial changes.
process: Brief
Agree the script, voice, editorial boundaries and intended use.
Record or assess
Review source audio or complete the approved recording session.
Edit and mix
Assemble dialogue and prepare the approved sound treatment.
Master
Review the complete programme and export the agreed versions.
faq: Does this include a particular voice artist?
Voice selection, artist availability, recording and usage rights are agreed before production. No specific performer or language coverage is assumed without confirmation.
Can you recreate someone’s voice with AI?
A voice replica requires explicit permission from the person or relevant rights holder. The method and permitted uses must be agreed; identity or endorsement is never implied without authority.
overview: Narration, dialogue editing, audio cleanup and podcast assembly.

title: Photography & videography
summary: Photography and video planned around the assets your business actually needs: product pages, campaigns, workplace stories or brand communications. We define coverage, organise the shoot and prepare selected images and footage for the agreed channels.
useCases: A product range needs consistent catalogue and campaign imagery.
A business needs original visuals instead of unrelated stock photography.
A launch needs photography and video captured in one coordinated production.

Location access, travel, releases and weather-dependent work are confirmed as production dependencies rather than left to the shoot day.
work.check: Approve the treatment, shot list and production responsibilities. Confirm product readiness, location permissions and participant availability.

work.detail: Photograph or film the agreed coverage with attention to lighting continuity, composition and usable framing. Check focus, exposure and sound where relevant during the session. Capture alternate crops or takes needed for the planned formats, and review representative material against the brief while reshooting is still possible.
work.check: Inspect sample captures at useful resolution. Confirm the shot list, technical quality and any missing coverage before ending production.

work.title: Selection, post-production and delivery
work.detail: Prepare a contact sheet or review selection, then complete the agreed retouching, colour treatment and video preparation. Exports match the required aspect ratios, sizes and channels. Usage licences, participant releases and the treatment of raw files are documented alongside the delivery and archive arrangements.
work.check: Review selected assets for colour consistency, unwanted artefacts and correct exports. Confirm filenames, usage permissions and the final approved selection.

technology.name: Capture, lighting and sound equipment
technology.detail: The equipment plan follows the subject, location and delivery requirement. Product detail, interviews and social footage require different lighting and recording approaches.

technology.name: Lightroom, Capture One and retouching workflows
technology.detail: Organised selections and consistent colour treatment support catalogue work. Retouching boundaries are agreed so images do not misrepresent a product or person.

technology.name: Video post-production and asset libraries
technology.detail: Footage can be prepared for a connected editing scope. Naming, metadata and delivery folders help marketing and design teams locate the right version.

Brand references, styling requirements and an approved shot list.
Location and participant permissions, plus confirmation of travel and production logistics.

Define coverage, visual direction and shoot dependencies.

Confirm access, products, people, equipment and the production schedule.
Capture
Complete the approved shot list with technical and creative checks.
Finish
Select, process and deliver the agreed assets and usage information.
faq: Can you provide on-location production everywhere?
Location, crew availability, access and travel are confirmed before an engagement is accepted. Remote coordination or client-supplied capture may suit some projects.
Are all raw files included?
The delivery specification identifies finished assets and whether raw files or source footage are included. Third-party rights and storage requirements also need to be agreed.
overview: Shot planning, original capture, selection, retouching and channel-ready assets.

useCases: A brand needs a recognisable audio signature or campaign theme.
A film or podcast needs music shaped around its edit and pacing.
Existing music needs arrangement, mixing or alternate versions for distribution.

work.detail: Review the audience, creative references, intended channels and the role of the music. Define mood, instrumentation, structure and duration without copying a reference composition. Confirm whether the brief requires original composition, licensed source material, performers or sample-based production, and identify the permissions each approach needs.
work.check: Approve the creative brief and reference interpretation. Record the intended uses, territories and rights responsibilities before production.

Revision checkpoints distinguish changes to the musical direction from refinements to an already approved arrangement.

work.detail: Balance the arrangement, manage dynamics and prepare masters for the agreed listening or distribution context. Produce scoped stems, loops, cut-downs and alternate mixes with clear naming. A delivery manifest identifies composition ownership, recording rights, performer permissions and any restrictions attached to licensed material.
work.check: Listen through the full master and edits, check loop boundaries and stem alignment, and verify the agreed formats and rights documentation.

technology.name: Digital audio workstations
technology.detail: Ableton Live, Logic Pro, Pro Tools or suitable equivalents support composition and production. Project compatibility matters when editable sessions form part of the handover.

technology.name: Recording, instruments and licensed libraries
technology.detail: The sound palette follows the approved brief. Samples, virtual instruments and recorded performances require permission appropriate to the proposed distribution and reuse.

technology.name: Mix and mastering workflows
technology.detail: Exports follow the destination requirements, including sample rate, bit depth, channel layout and any platform loudness specification. Separate formats are checked independently.

Agreed stems, loops and alternate edits
inputs: The intended channels, durations, audience and creative references.
Picture edits or timing requirements, plus source sessions where relevant.
An approver for musical direction and agreement on composition, recording and performance rights.

Agree musical direction, intended uses and rights requirements.
Demo
Review the theme, arrangement direction and picture timing.

Complete the approved arrangement, recording and mix.
Master and hand over
Check final versions and package the agreed rights and source materials.
faq: Will we own the music?
Ownership and permitted uses are specified in the agreement. Composition, recording, performance and third-party sample rights can be separate and must all support the intended use.
Can you make music that sounds exactly like an existing song?
References can guide qualities such as energy or instrumentation, but the composition must be original or appropriately licensed. We do not promise a copy of protected work.
overview: Original composition, arrangement, mixing, mastering and audio-brand assets.

title: Copywriting, blogging & ghostwriting

summary: Website copy, articles and longer-form writing developed from your brief, source material and subject expertise. We establish the reader, voice and structure before drafting, then review factual claims and edit the work for publication under the agreed authorship arrangement.
useCases: A website explains features without making the offer understandable.
A subject expert needs help turning interviews or notes into a coherent article.
An author or leader needs editorial support that preserves their own perspective.

Build an outline and evidence register, with unresolved questions separated from facts that can be stated confidently.
work.check: Approve the outline, tone examples and source requirements. Confirm attribution, confidentiality and who owns factual review.

work.title: Drafting and substantive editing
work.detail: Develop the argument or narrative using the approved structure and source material. Replace unsupported generalities with explanations, examples and evidence that the client can substantiate. For ghostwritten work, drafts are reviewed for the named author’s meaning and voice; credentials, personal experience and client results are never invented.
work.check: Review accuracy, narrative order, originality and alignment with the brief. Resolve claims and quotations with the author or subject owner.

work.title: Copy editing and publication preparation
work.detail: Refine sentence structure, terminology, headings and transitions. Prepare the agreed metadata, calls to action or author notes and check links and citations. A final clean version and an editorial query log make publication decisions clear, including any source or permission issues that still need approval.
work.check: Proofread the publication version, check references and confirm approval of the final wording, attribution and destination.

technology.name: Interviews, outlines and evidence registers
technology.detail: A structured source process provides the detail that distinguishes original writing from generic summaries. Notes remain connected to the claims they support.

technology.name: Collaborative editing and version control
technology.detail: Tracked revisions, comments and named versions help consolidate feedback. Confidential interview or manuscript material uses the agreed storage and access controls.

technology.name: Publishing and editorial checks
technology.detail: Website copy can be prepared for a CMS; articles or manuscripts follow their destination style guide. Terminology, links and citations are checked before delivery.

deliverables: Headings, metadata or author notes where included
inputs: The intended audience, format, publication destination and desired reader action.
Reliable source material, relevant interviews and permission to use supplied examples.
The named author or subject reviewer, authorship terms and a consolidated feedback owner.

Agree the audience, source material, voice and publication purpose.
Outline
Resolve the structure and evidence requirements before drafting.
Draft and revise
Develop the piece and review meaning and factual accuracy.
Prepare publication
Complete the edit, references and approved final version.
faq: Can you write in our founder’s voice?
We use writing samples, interviews and their review to establish the voice. The founder remains responsible for confirming personal statements, experiences and viewpoints attributed to them.
How does this avoid generic AI-style writing?

The process starts with specific source material, an editorial point of view and factual review. Concrete examples, useful structure and careful editing matter more than adding impressive-sounding language.
overview: Website copy, articles and authored material built from real source expertise.

title: Translation & localisation
summary: Adapt content for the language, audience and interface where it will be used. We define the language pair, terminology and review requirements, then manage translation, contextual editing and delivery in the formats your publishing or product team needs.
useCases: A website or application is being prepared for another language or region.
Product or marketing content needs consistent terminology across translated assets.
Existing translations are accurate word by word but awkward or unsuitable in context.

work.title: Language scope, terminology and context
work.detail: Confirm the source and target languages, regional variant, intended audience and specialist subject matter. Build a glossary and style guidance from approved terminology. Interface screenshots, placeholders and content constraints are supplied alongside strings so the translation can reflect actual use rather than isolated fragments.
work.check: Approve the language scope, glossary, reference tone and specialist review needs. Identify strings that must remain unchanged.

work.title: Translation and contextual adaptation
work.detail: Translate the agreed content and adapt idiom, examples, dates, units and tone where the brief requires localisation. Preserve names, variables, links and product meaning. Questions about ambiguous source material are logged for resolution; legal, medical or other specialist material requires the relevant reviewer and is scoped accordingly.
work.check: Check completeness, terminology, source meaning and preservation of placeholders. Resolve source ambiguities and record approved local adaptations.

work.title: Linguistic and in-context quality review
work.detail: Review the translated copy in its destination format. For interfaces, inspect overflow, truncation, line breaks, directionality and locale-specific formatting with the product team. Deliver a versioned package and glossary updates so subsequent changes can remain consistent with the approved translation.
work.check: Compare the delivered files with the source inventory, test representative screens and confirm the language reviewer’s approval and remaining layout issues.

technology.name: Glossaries and translation memory
technology.detail: Approved terms and reusable segments support consistency across related files. Client-owned terminology and previously approved translations are assessed before introducing new wording.

technology.name: Localisation files and content systems
technology.detail: JSON, XLIFF, PO files, spreadsheets or CMS exports can be used according to the product. Encoding, placeholders and string identifiers must survive the round trip.

technology.name: Linguistic and interface QA
technology.detail: Contextual review checks meaning and presentation together. Language support, reviewer availability and right-to-left requirements are confirmed before committing to delivery.

inputs: Editable source material, target locales and confirmation of available source rights.
Product context, glossary, screenshots and placeholder or character constraints.
A suitable language reviewer, publication owner and any certification requirements.
process: Scope
Confirm languages, formats, specialist requirements and reviewer availability.
Prepare
Establish terminology and resolve source-content questions.
Translate and review
Develop the target copy and check meaning and consistency.
Validate in context
Inspect the destination format and deliver the approved package.
faq: Do you cover every language?
Language pairs, specialist competence and reviewer availability are confirmed before work is accepted. We do not assume coverage or certification that has not been established.
Is certified translation included?
Only when the required certification, jurisdiction and authorised professional have been confirmed in the scope. Standard localisation is not presented as a certified legal translation.
overview: Contextual translation, terminology management and in-product language checks.

title: Transcription & subtitling
summary: Turn spoken recordings into usable transcripts, captions and subtitles. We agree the transcription style, speaker treatment and delivery format, then review the text against the audio and align timed output with the actual viewing experience.
useCases: Interviews or meetings need a readable, searchable written record.
Video content needs captions for accessibility or sound-off viewing.
A publication or production team needs timecoded source text for editing.

work.title: Recording assessment and output rules
work.detail: Review duration, recording quality, languages, speaker count and subject terminology. Agree verbatim, intelligent-verbatim or edited transcription, including how to handle interruptions, non-speech sounds and unclear passages. Translation is treated as a separate requirement rather than silently added to a transcription brief.
work.check: Check representative audio and approve the transcription conventions, speaker identification and required timing precision.

work.title: Transcription, speaker identification and verification
work.detail: Produce the transcript, identify speakers where the recording allows it and verify important names, numbers and technical terms. Automated tools can support a first pass when authorised, but uncertain content is reviewed and marked. Missing or unintelligible speech is not filled with invented wording.
work.check: Compare the transcript with the recording, review speaker changes and inspect terms or passages flagged as uncertain.

work.title: Subtitle timing and delivery quality
work.detail: Create timecoded captions or subtitles with readable segmentation, suitable line breaks and the agreed treatment of sound cues. Check synchronisation with speech and the destination player’s requirements. Deliver editable text and timed files with a clear version identifier and a record of unresolved source limitations.
work.check: Play the captioned programme, inspect timing and reading flow, and verify that the final files import into the agreed editing or publishing system.

technology.name: Audio review and transcript editing
technology.detail: Playback controls, timecodes and terminology lists support verification. Confidential recordings use the agreed processing environment and retention rules.

technology.name: SRT, WebVTT and production formats
technology.detail: Timed-text formats follow the destination player or editor. Text encoding and timestamp syntax are checked as well as the visible wording.

technology.name: Caption and accessibility review
technology.detail: Captions may include meaningful sound information; subtitles may follow different editorial rules. The chosen standard and coverage are stated in the brief.

deliverables: Transcript in the agreed editorial style
Speaker labels and timestamps where included
inputs: Original recordings or the highest-quality source available, with permission to process them.
Speaker names where known, terminology lists and the intended publication context.
Required language, transcript style, caption format and confidentiality requirements.
process: Assess
Review recording quality and agree the editorial and timing rules.
Transcribe
Develop and verify the text against the recording.
Time and format
Prepare captions or subtitles for the target player.
Review
Check complete playback and deliver the approved text and timed files.
faq: Can you transcribe poor audio perfectly?
No. Background noise, overlapping speech or missing audio can limit accuracy. We assess a sample, flag uncertain passages and explain where a better source is needed.
Does subtitling include translation?
Same-language captions and translated subtitles are different scopes. A translated version needs confirmed language support and linguistic review as well as timing work.
overview: Verified transcripts, speaker labels, timed captions and subtitle files.

title: CV, résumé & LinkedIn writing
summary: Present your experience clearly for the roles you intend to pursue. We organise your work history, develop evidence-based achievement statements and prepare an editable CV and scoped LinkedIn profile copy, with every qualification and claim reviewed by you.
useCases: Your CV lists duties without explaining relevant contributions or outcomes.
You are changing roles and need to make transferable experience clear.
Your LinkedIn profile and application documents tell inconsistent professional stories.

work.title: Career evidence and target-role review
work.detail: Review your existing documents, work history and representative role descriptions. Identify responsibilities, projects, tools and outcomes relevant to the target. Ask for context behind claims and separate measured results from estimates. Gaps or transitions are handled accurately rather than hidden with invented employment or qualifications.
work.check: Confirm dates, titles, employers, qualifications and the evidence supporting proposed achievement statements before drafting.

work.title: CV structure and profile writing
work.detail: Develop a clear hierarchy for the summary, experience, projects, skills and education. Use relevant terminology naturally and make the document readable for both recruiters and common application systems. LinkedIn copy follows the platform’s sections while preserving your actual seniority, contribution and professional voice.
work.check: Compare the draft with target-role requirements, verify factual statements and check that the most relevant evidence is easy to find.

work.title: Document formatting and handover
work.detail: Prepare the agreed editable and PDF versions with consistent typography, headings and contact details. Inspect text extraction and page flow rather than relying on a decorative template. Profile changes are supplied as approved copy; account passwords and personal-profile access are not required for writing the material.
work.check: Proofread every version, test links and text selection, and obtain your approval of the final employment and achievement claims.

technology.name: Structured career interviews
technology.detail: A focused evidence-gathering process turns project details and responsibilities into accurate achievement statements without manufacturing numbers or credentials.

technology.name: Word, Google Docs and PDF delivery
technology.detail: The document format follows the application context. Simple structures, consistent headings and usable text are preferred where machine parsing matters.

technology.name: Role and keyword mapping
technology.detail: Representative role descriptions guide relevance and terminology. Keyword use supports clarity and fit; no formatting method guarantees screening or an interview.

deliverables: CV or résumé in agreed editable and PDF formats
Scoped LinkedIn headline, about and experience copy
inputs: Your existing CV, work history, qualification details and accurate contact information.
Representative target roles and examples of projects or contributions you can substantiate.
Confirmation of confidential work restrictions and personal approval of all career claims.
process: Gather evidence
Review your background and target roles in detail.
Position
Select the experience and terminology most relevant to the intended applications.
Write and review
Draft the documents and resolve factual questions with you.
Format and deliver
Check the editable files, PDF output and agreed profile copy.
faq: Do you guarantee a job or an interview?
No. The service improves the accuracy, relevance and presentation of your material. Employer decisions depend on the role, applicant pool and hiring process.
Will you add impressive achievements if I have no numbers?
No. We can describe scope, complexity and contribution without inventing metrics. Any estimate must be clearly supportable and approved by you.
overview: Evidence-led CVs, achievement statements and consistent LinkedIn profile copy.

title: Technical writing & documentation
summary: Documentation developed from the product, source systems and the tasks readers need to complete. We create the agreed API references, setup guides, operating procedures or user documentation, with runnable examples, review ownership and a practical update process.
useCases: Users rely on undocumented setup steps or repeated support explanations.
An API needs consistent references and verified integration examples.
A system handover needs operating instructions that another team can follow.

work.title: Reader tasks and documentation architecture
work.detail: Identify the audiences, prerequisites and tasks the documentation must support. Inventory existing material and map gaps across tutorials, how-to guides, conceptual explanations and reference content. Establish terminology, version scope and the source of truth so contradictory pages are resolved before more content is added.
work.check: Approve the document map and priority reader journeys. Confirm access to the product, technical reviewers and a suitable test environment.

work.title: Writing and technical verification
work.detail: Develop instructions from observed product behaviour and approved engineering sources. API material covers authentication, request and response fields, errors and example calls. Procedures identify prerequisites, commands, expected results and recovery steps. Examples use safe placeholder values and do not expose credentials or customer data.
work.check: Run agreed examples in the stated environment, verify outputs and have the responsible technical owner review accuracy and limitations.

work.title: Publishing and maintenance workflow
work.detail: Prepare content for the chosen documentation platform with consistent navigation, code formatting and cross-links. Define how releases trigger a documentation review and how obsolete instructions are archived or redirected. Handover includes authoring conventions, reviewer responsibilities and the known gaps still awaiting product decisions.
work.check: Check links, searchability and version labels. Have a representative reader follow a priority task without relying on undocumented assistance.

technology.name: Markdown and documentation platforms
technology.detail: Version-controlled documentation or a managed knowledge base can support review and publishing. The choice follows ownership, permissions and the release workflow.

technology.name: OpenAPI and API examples
technology.detail: Existing schemas and API contracts can inform reference material. Generated references still need useful explanations, tested examples and clear treatment of authentication and errors.

technology.name: Diagrams and operating runbooks
technology.detail: Architecture views, data-flow diagrams and step-by-step procedures make responsibilities and dependencies visible. Diagrams are checked against the actual system and version.

inputs: Access to the relevant product, source material and a safe technical test environment.
API contracts, architecture information and a named subject-matter reviewer.
Target readers, supported versions and the publishing and maintenance owner.
process: Map the tasks
Agree audiences, document types and priority gaps.
Inspect and draft
Use the product and technical sources to write the material.
Verify
Test examples and complete subject-matter review.
Publish and maintain
Deliver the approved content and an update workflow.
faq: Can you document an unfinished product?
Yes, with versioned assumptions and close engineering review. Unimplemented behaviour must be identified rather than described as an available feature.
Do you need repository access?
Only when required for the scoped material. Demonstrations, schemas and a test environment may be sufficient; access is limited to what the documentation work needs.
overview: API references, setup guides, operating runbooks and verified examples.

title: Virtual assistance & administration
summary: Administrative support for the recurring work that keeps your business organised: scheduling, records, document preparation, inbox triage and approved follow-up. Tasks are delivered through defined procedures, access permissions and escalation rules rather than an open-ended list of responsibilities.
useCases: Routine administration takes time away from client delivery or leadership.
Scheduling, records and follow-up depend on one person’s memory.
A growing team needs a documented handover for recurring administrative work.

work.title: Task inventory and operating procedures
work.detail: Identify recurring tasks, expected volumes, deadlines and the systems involved. Document what a completed task looks like, which decisions require approval and which exceptions should be escalated. Begin with a defined set of responsibilities so access and performance can be reviewed before the service expands.
work.check: Approve the task list, completion criteria and escalation rules. Confirm the owner and priority for each recurring activity.

work.title: Administration and controlled execution
work.detail: Carry out the agreed scheduling, record updates, document formatting, inbox triage or follow-up work using business-owned tools. Calendar actions, external messages, purchases and changes involving sensitive information follow the stated approval rules. Work is recorded so the business can see what was completed and what remains blocked.
work.check: Check representative records and outputs against the procedure. Verify destinations, dates and approvals before consequential actions are taken.

work.title: Quality review and continuity
work.detail: Use periodic checks to identify recurring exceptions, missing inputs and opportunities to improve the procedure. Maintain an accessible task and issue register, document updates and prepare a continuity handover. Availability, working hours, turnaround expectations and backup arrangements are agreed explicitly.
work.check: Review task completion, error corrections and escalation response. Confirm that another authorised person can follow the documented procedure.

technology.name: Business email and calendars
technology.detail: Use delegated access or approved shared inboxes rather than personal password sharing. Ownership and external communication permissions remain with the business.

technology.name: Microsoft 365, Google Workspace and task systems
technology.detail: Shared documents, spreadsheets and work queues keep routine operations visible. Folder permissions, naming and document versions are included in the procedure.

technology.name: SOPs and quality checklists
technology.detail: Task-specific instructions define inputs, steps, outputs and exceptions. Suitable recurring steps can later be considered for automation without assuming every task should be automated.

inputs: A prioritised task list, expected volumes, deadlines and operating hours.
Authorised tool access and clear rules for external communication and sensitive information.
An approval contact, escalation route and examples of correctly completed work.
process: Define
Select the initial tasks and completion standards.
Document
Confirm procedures, access and escalation rules.
Operate
Complete the agreed work and record exceptions.
Review
Check quality and refine responsibilities before expanding scope.
faq: Can you manage every administrative task?
The engagement defines the tasks, systems and authority provided. Financial commitments, legal decisions and other consequential actions need the appropriate business approver.
Will you need my personal passwords?
Access should use business-controlled delegation or suitable account permissions wherever available. Credential handling and offboarding are agreed before work begins.
overview: Scheduling, records, document preparation and approved administrative follow-up.

title: Bookkeeping, accounting & tax support
summary: Organise financial records, reconcile transactions and prepare reporting or tax-filing work for the relevant business and jurisdiction. Before accepting an engagement, we confirm the required professional credentials, authorised filing role, reporting basis and responsibilities for review and submission.
useCases: Transactions and supporting documents are not ready for a reliable period close.
A business needs a structured handover to its accountant or tax adviser.
Filing preparation requires a clear record of source data, queries and approvals.

work.title: Engagement and records assessment
work.detail: Confirm the legal entity, jurisdiction, reporting period, accounting basis and professional requirements. Inventory bank, sales, purchasing and payroll-related records within scope. Identify missing evidence and prior-period issues before processing begins; statutory advice, audit and authorised filing are distinguished from routine bookkeeping work.
work.check: Confirm professional suitability and permitted responsibilities. Approve the source inventory, period boundaries and outstanding-document list.

work.title: Bookkeeping, reconciliation and close support
work.detail: Process the agreed transaction records using an approved chart of accounts and documented classification rules. Reconcile bank and control-account balances to supporting evidence, investigate discrepancies and prepare a query log. Adjustments that require judgement are routed to the responsible reviewer rather than silently posted as settled conclusions.
work.check: Reconcile selected balances to source statements, check duplicate and missing entries, and obtain approval for material corrections and unresolved classifications.

work.title: Reporting and tax-filing coordination
work.detail: Prepare the agreed financial schedules, management reports or filing-support package with traceable source references. Jurisdiction-specific tax treatment and statutory submissions require the confirmed appropriately qualified or authorised professional. Review, client approval, submission responsibility and any filing acknowledgement are documented before the engagement is considered complete.
work.check: Verify report periods and reconciliations, resolve reviewer queries and retain the required approval or submission evidence for the scoped work.

technology.name: Accounting platforms and controlled imports
technology.detail: QuickBooks, Xero or an appropriate existing system can support transaction processing. Account structure, currency, period locks and import mapping need review before bulk changes.

technology.name: Reconciliation and document registers
technology.detail: Supporting statements and invoices are linked to reconciliation schedules and exceptions. Access is restricted because financial records contain sensitive commercial and personal information.

technology.name: Reporting and filing systems
technology.detail: The applicable jurisdiction determines reporting formats and filing access. Tool availability does not establish professional authority to provide regulated advice or submit returns.

deliverables: Reviewer approval and submission records where included
inputs: Entity details, jurisdiction, reporting period and the required accounting or filing scope.
Authorised access to complete source records and prior-period balances where relevant.
Confirmation of the responsible qualified professional, client approver and submission authority.
process: Confirm the engagement
Establish jurisdiction, professional requirements and responsibility boundaries.
Collect and reconcile
Review evidence and prepare the agreed accounting records.
Review
Resolve classification, reconciliation and reporting queries with the responsible reviewer.
Complete the period
Deliver the approved reports or coordinate the authorised filing and handover.
faq: Can you file taxes in any country?
No jurisdiction or filing authority is assumed. The country, entity type, required credentials and authorised professional must be confirmed before filing work is accepted.
Is this an audit or assurance opinion?

No. Bookkeeping, reporting support and filing preparation do not constitute statutory audit or independent assurance. Those services need a separately defined engagement and appropriately authorised provider.
overview: Reconciled records, close support and jurisdiction-specific filing coordination.

title: Business consulting & coaching
summary: Structured support for a defined business problem: an unclear offer, an inefficient operating process, a new service or a delivery constraint. We develop the diagnosis, decision options and implementation plan with the people responsible for acting on it.
useCases: A business decision is stalled by unclear assumptions or competing priorities.
Growth has exposed gaps in ownership, workflow or customer experience.
A founder or manager needs a structured review and follow-through process.

work.title: Problem definition and operating diagnosis
work.detail: Review the business question, available records, stakeholder perspectives and existing operating process. Define the baseline and distinguish symptoms from possible causes. Interviews, process mapping or market evidence are included where useful; the diagnosis records what is known, assumed and still uncertain.
work.check: Agree the problem statement, evidence sources and decision criteria. Review the baseline and the assumptions that most affect the conclusion.

work.title: Options, priorities and practical recommendations
work.detail: Develop a small set of workable options with dependencies, trade-offs and implications for people, systems and delivery. Recommendations identify the responsible owner and the evidence behind the decision. Financial modelling or specialist legal and tax analysis is a separate requirement when the question needs it.
work.check: Compare options against the agreed criteria and resource constraints. Confirm which assumptions require validation before committing to a direction.

work.title: Implementation support and coaching
work.detail: Translate the selected direction into actions, milestones and review points. Coaching sessions can support the named manager’s decisions and working practices, with agreed preparation and follow-up. Progress reviews focus on completed actions, observed operating changes and unresolved blockers rather than motivational language or guaranteed growth claims.
work.check: Review action ownership, milestone evidence and the measures selected for the change. Record decisions and adjust the plan when assumptions no longer hold.

technology.name: Process mapping and stakeholder interviews
technology.detail: Visualise handoffs, responsibilities and recurring exceptions. Use actual operating evidence rather than assuming a standard framework explains every business.

technology.name: Decision models and scenario analysis
technology.detail: Document assumptions and compare options using suitable spreadsheets or analysis tools. Models support decisions; their outputs remain limited by the quality of inputs.

technology.name: Action and review systems
technology.detail: An action register, decision log and review cadence connect the recommendation to execution. Existing project tools can be used to avoid creating another disconnected reporting layer.

deliverables: Review notes and updated action register
inputs: A specific business question, relevant operating records and decision context.
Access to the people responsible for the process and the authority to validate assumptions.
An accountable decision-maker and agreement on what implementation support includes.
process: Frame
Define the problem, baseline and decision criteria.
Diagnose
Examine evidence and test the important assumptions.
Decide
Review options and agree a practical direction.
Implement and review
Track actions, changes and unresolved blockers.
faq: Do you guarantee business growth?
No. We define the analysis, recommendations and implementation support. Commercial outcomes depend on execution, market conditions and decisions outside the engagement.
How is coaching different from consulting?
Consulting develops analysis and recommendations for a defined problem. Coaching supports an individual’s decision-making and follow-through; the scope states which approach is being provided.
overview: Operating diagnosis, decision options, implementation plans and management coaching.

title: Legal services, contracts & compliance
summary: Scope legal, contract and compliance work around the relevant jurisdiction, business activity and authorised professional. The engagement may cover document preparation, contract-review coordination and compliance operations; legal advice and regulated work begin only after the appropriate qualifications and engagement terms are confirmed.
useCases: A business needs a controlled process for preparing and reviewing commercial contracts.
A new activity needs its legal questions and compliance obligations identified.
Existing agreements and policies lack clear ownership, versions or review records.

work.title: Jurisdiction, authority and engagement

Identify the required legal qualifications and permitted work, check the engagement and confidentiality arrangements, and establish who may provide advice or represent the business. Administrative support is distinguished from regulated legal practice.
work.check: Confirm the responsible appropriately qualified professional and accepted engagement before substantive advice, representation or regulated document work begins.

work.title: Contract and document workflow
work.detail: Collect instructions, existing agreements and the commercial positions to be reviewed. Prepare the scoped document pack or coordinate clause review, redlines, questions and approval status. Version control records whose wording was approved; signing authority and negotiation decisions remain with the designated client representative and legal professional.
work.check: Check party details, version history and unresolved review points. Obtain the required legal and business approvals before documents are presented for signature.

work.title: Compliance operations and handover
work.detail: Map the agreed obligations or policy requirements to owners, evidence, review dates and operating procedures under the professional’s direction. Organise policy updates, registers and follow-up tasks. The output identifies open legal questions and dependencies; a checklist or drafted policy is not represented as a blanket assurance of compliance.
work.check: Review the evidence register, responsibilities and outstanding questions with the authorised reviewer. Record the approved documents and next review dates.

technology.name: Document comparison and version control
technology.detail: Tracked changes and a controlled document register support contract review. Confidential material is shared only through the agreed access and storage arrangements.

technology.name: Contract and policy registers
technology.detail: Record parties, status, authority, renewal or review dates and the responsible owner. Workflow tools organise legal operations without replacing professional judgement.

technology.name: Jurisdiction-specific research and review
technology.detail: The relevant qualified professional determines the applicable legal sources and advice. No universal template or automated drafting tool establishes legal suitability on its own.

deliverables: Scoped draft or reviewed document pack
Handover with open issues and review dates
inputs: The relevant jurisdictions, legal entity, business activity and the question requiring review.
Complete source documents, commercial instructions and authority to share confidential material.
Confirmation of the appropriately qualified professional, client approver and signing authority.
process: Establish suitability
Confirm jurisdiction, professional authority and accepted engagement terms.
Collect instructions
Review source documents and the client’s intended commercial position.
Prepare and review
Complete the scoped work with the authorised professional and approvers.
Handover
Deliver approved versions, outstanding questions and review responsibilities.
faq: Can you provide legal advice in every jurisdiction?

No. Availability depends on the jurisdiction, subject matter and confirmed professional qualifications. Work is accepted only after the appropriate scope and authorised provider have been established.
Will a policy template make our business compliant?
A document alone does not establish compliance. The applicable requirements, operating practices, evidence and professional review must be considered for the specific business and jurisdiction.
overview: Jurisdiction-scoped contracts, professional review and compliance operations.

Employee onboarding or HR administration needs a repeatable operating process.

work.detail: Prepare the agreed role material and manage authorised sourcing or application channels. work.title: HR administration and onboarding handover
work.detail: Coordinate the scoped offer, onboarding checklist, access requests, document collection and employee record updates under client direction. Contract wording, employment-law questions and payroll decisions are routed to the relevant authorised professional. Handover makes ongoing responsibilities, review dates and offboarding requirements explicit.
work.check: Review document completion, access ownership and outstanding onboarding tasks. Confirm candidate and employee data is retained or removed under the agreed policy.

technology.name: Applicant tracking and scheduling systems
technology.detail: A suitable ATS or controlled shared workflow tracks applications, stages, communications and access. Candidate information should not be scattered across unrestricted spreadsheets and inboxes.

technology.name: Job-related assessment frameworks
technology.detail: Structured criteria and interview scorecards support consistent human review. Automated tools can organise information but do not replace accountable hiring decisions.

technology.name: HRIS and onboarding checklists
technology.detail: The agreed HR platform can maintain employee records and recurring tasks. Permissions and required fields follow the organisation’s actual operating and privacy requirements.

inputs: Role requirements, working arrangements and authorised hiring decision-makers.
Approved sourcing channels, applicant privacy information and retention requirements.
HR policies, the relevant jurisdiction and contacts for employment-law or payroll questions.
process: Define the role
Agree the responsibilities, requirements and assessment process.
Prepare the workflow
Set up channels, records, access and candidate communications.
Coordinate
Support the agreed sourcing, interviews and human review stages.
Handover
Complete onboarding coordination and transfer ongoing HR responsibilities.

No. We support the agreed recruitment process. Final employment decisions remain with the business’s authorised human decision-makers.
Does HR outsourcing include employment-law advice?
Not automatically. Jurisdiction-specific legal work and regulated advice need the relevant qualified professional and an explicitly agreed engagement.
overview: Role briefs, applicant coordination, interview workflows and HR administration.

summary: A defined customer-support operation for the channels and hours your business needs. We organise queues, knowledge, response guidance and escalation so enquiries can be handled consistently, with staffing, languages and service targets confirmed before the operation begins.

A team needs structured support during growth or a product launch.
Repeated issues need better knowledge articles and escalation to the product team.

work.detail: Review contact volumes, reasons for contact, supported channels and the systems agents must use. Define service hours, language needs, identity-verification steps and escalation boundaries. Refunds, account changes, commitments and sensitive cases need explicit authority; staffing and response targets are confirmed from the actual operating requirements.
work.check: Approve the channel coverage, authority matrix and escalation procedure. Confirm that access and knowledge are sufficient for the included contact types.

work.detail: Build or refine response guidance, knowledge articles, ticket categories and assignment rules. Prepare agents for representative scenarios using approved test or anonymised cases. Scripts support consistent information but should not prevent escalation when a situation falls outside the documented policy.
work.check: Review sample responses, test routing and verify that agents can identify cases requiring a specialist or manager.

work.title: Operations, quality review and reporting
work.detail: Handle the agreed contacts and maintain case notes, status and ownership. Sample interactions for accuracy, clarity and policy adherence, then feed recurring issues back to the responsible business team. Reporting distinguishes response time, resolution, backlog and customer feedback rather than reducing quality to conversation volume.
work.check: Check sampled cases and escalations, review unresolved backlog and confirm that corrections are reflected in knowledge and operating procedures.

technology.name: Helpdesk and omnichannel systems
technology.detail: Zendesk, Freshdesk, Intercom or your existing system can support queues and case history. Channel availability and integrations are confirmed against the required workflow.

technology.name: Telephony and call recording
technology.detail: Call-centre work requires suitable numbers, routing, staffing and call-handling permissions. Recording, disclosures and retention follow the applicable market and approved policy.

technology.name: Knowledge bases and quality scorecards
technology.detail: Versioned answers, escalation guides and review criteria make service quality assessable. Article ownership and update triggers prevent outdated advice from becoming standard practice.

Agent preparation and scenario review records
Operational issue log and improvement recommendations
inputs: Supported products, channels, languages, hours and expected contact volumes.
Approved customer policies, account-access rules and authority for refunds or account changes.
Helpdesk access, escalation contacts and the applicable recording and privacy requirements.
process: Design
Agree contact scope, coverage, authority and service measures.
Prepare
Configure queues and develop the knowledge and training material.
Launch
Start the approved operation with monitored handoffs and escalations.
Improve
Review quality, recurring issues and backlog with the business owner.

Coverage, staffing and language competence must be confirmed before commitment. No round-the-clock or multilingual capability is assumed from a general service listing.
Can agents issue refunds or change accounts?
Only within documented authority and verification rules. Cases beyond those limits are escalated to the authorised business contact.
overview: Support queues, knowledge, escalation rules and quality-reviewed service operations.

title: Project management & delivery coordination
summary: Project coordination that makes scope, decisions and next actions visible. We establish the delivery plan, responsibilities and reporting, then manage the agreed dependencies, reviews and change process so the people doing the work can move forward with clear decisions.
useCases: Several suppliers or internal teams are working without a shared delivery plan.
Projects drift because decisions, dependencies and scope changes are not recorded.
A launch needs coordinated acceptance, handover and operational readiness.

work.title: Project definition and delivery planning
work.detail: Review the intended outcome, deliverables, stakeholders and constraints. Break the work into reviewable milestones, identify dependencies and establish decision and escalation roles. The plan records assumptions and external commitments rather than treating a target date as evidence that every dependency can be met.
work.check: Approve the scope baseline, responsibility map, milestones and acceptance process. Identify unresolved dependencies and who can make the necessary decisions.

work.title: Coordination, reporting and change control
work.detail: Maintain the delivery board, action register and decision log. Facilitate the agreed planning and review sessions, track blockers and make trade-offs visible early. Changes are assessed for their effect on scope, effort and dependencies before they become commitments; status reporting distinguishes completed work from activity.
work.check: Check milestone evidence, action ownership and overdue decisions. Record approved changes and communicate the revised delivery baseline.

work.title: Acceptance, release and transition
work.detail: Coordinate acceptance against the agreed criteria and prepare the handover checklist, operating responsibilities and outstanding-issue register. A release decision considers readiness across the workstreams, including documentation, access and support. Closeout identifies what has been accepted and what remains with a named owner.
work.check: Review acceptance evidence and unresolved risks with the decision-maker. Confirm handover materials, account ownership and post-release responsibilities.

technology.name: Jira, Linear, Asana or existing project systems
technology.detail: Use one agreed source of truth for tasks, owners and status. The tool should support the team’s delivery method rather than introduce a parallel reporting burden.

technology.name: Dependency and decision registers
technology.detail: Track assumptions, risks, decisions and external commitments separately from the task list. Each item needs an owner and a useful review or due date.

technology.name: Acceptance and handover checklists
technology.detail: Document evidence for completion and operational readiness. A task marked done is not automatically an accepted deliverable or a releasable system.

inputs: The intended outcome, deliverable list and current project status.
Access to workstream owners, supplier commitments and relevant project records.
A decision-maker with authority over priorities, changes and acceptance.

Agree scope, ownership, milestones and acceptance criteria.
Coordinate
Maintain the plan and resolve decisions and dependencies.
Review
Inspect deliverables and manage approved changes.
Transition
Complete acceptance, handover and ownership of remaining work.

Can you join a project already in progress?
