overview: Scope, milestones, dependencies, decision records and coordinated handover.

title: Market research & customer insight
summary: Research designed around a decision, with a defined audience, method and evidence standard. We investigate customer needs, competing alternatives and market conditions, then translate the findings into implications your team can use without overstating what the sample proves.
useCases: A new offer needs evidence before positioning or product investment.
Customer feedback is anecdotal and difficult to compare.
A business needs a clearer view of competitors, segments or purchasing criteria.

work.title: Research question and method design
work.detail: Define the decision, target population, existing evidence and what remains uncertain. Choose suitable desk research, interviews, surveys or a combination, with a recruitment plan and discussion or questionnaire structure. Sampling limitations, respondent privacy and the treatment of incentives are recorded before collection begins.
work.check: Approve the research questions, target participants and method. Review the instrument for leading questions, missing context and unsuitable personal-data collection.

work.title: Evidence collection and analysis
work.detail: Collect the agreed primary or secondary material and preserve source references. Qualitative analysis identifies patterns and exceptions without presenting a few interviews as a statistically representative market. Quantitative work states sample size, definitions and exclusions; competitor comparisons distinguish published claims from independently verified facts.
work.check: Review source quality and respondent suitability, verify coding or calculations and investigate contradictory findings rather than removing them for a cleaner narrative.

work.title: Findings, implications and decision support
work.detail: Organise the evidence around the original decision. Present customer needs, alternatives and implications with an explicit separation between findings, interpretation and recommendations. A useful handover includes source material, method notes and further questions so the business can revisit the conclusion when conditions change.
work.check: Trace key conclusions to evidence, check whether uncertainty is stated and review the recommended next actions with the decision owner.

technology.name: Interview and survey workflows
technology.detail: Discussion guides, consent procedures and suitable research platforms support consistent collection. Recruitment quality matters as much as the number of responses.

technology.name: Desk research and source registers
technology.detail: Document publication date, geography, definitions and source authority. Published market estimates are compared carefully when their methods or populations differ.

technology.name: Qualitative coding and analytical reporting
technology.detail: Use structured coding, spreadsheets or statistical tools suited to the method. Findings remain connected to source evidence, with personal information restricted or anonymised as agreed.

deliverables: Source register and scoped evidence collection
Analysis with sample and method limitations
inputs: The business decision, target markets and existing research or customer feedback.
Approved recruitment channels and permission to contact any supplied participants.
A decision owner, data-handling requirements and access to relevant subject experts.
process: Frame the decision
Agree research questions, audience and evidence requirements.
Design
Prepare the method, sample approach and collection instruments.
Collect and analyse
Gather evidence and examine patterns, exceptions and limitations.
Interpret
Review implications and next actions with the decision-maker.
faq: Can you calculate the exact size of any market?
Only where the evidence and definitions support a defensible estimate. We state methods, assumptions and ranges instead of turning uncertain source data into a precise-looking number.
Is desk research enough?
Sometimes. It depends on the decision and the available sources. Customer interviews or surveys may be needed when published information cannot answer the important questions.
overview: Customer interviews, desk research, surveys and evidence-based decision reports.
